summary: A liverwort common across the Northern Hemisphere and widely distributed in Canada. It has a strongly scented, dark green leathery surface with purplish margins, though the name belongs to a complex containing several visually indistinguishable species.
A moss native to Eurasia and North America. It is a terrestrial, long-lived plant associated with woodlands and pioneer vegetation.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is recorded parasitising Retama sphaerocarpa, Dittrichia viscosa and species of Tamarix.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering perennial native to Albania, Bulgaria, Greece and Yugoslavia, this hellebore has basal, palm-shaped green leaves and leafless flower stalks. Its flowers are green to yellow-green.
A bulb-growing plant native from southern Europe to northern Iraq. It produces bluish-purple flowers in March and April on tall flowering stalks.

A summer-growing bulbous plant native to southern Africa from Zimbabwe through Malawi to South Africa’s Limpopo Province. Its sweetly scented white flowers turn green later and form a loose spike topped by a tuft of short pointed bracts.

A grapevine native to Asia, the Amur grape withstands severe frost but not drought. Its berries range from very acidic to sweet, and ripe fruit can be eaten raw or made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; the leaves are used in salad.
edibilityNote: Ripe grapes are eaten raw; unripe fruit is acidic and bitter. Fruit is made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; leaves are used in salad.

summary: Flowering plant native to central Europe and the Mediterranean region, it has a flattened oval bulb surrounded by many tiny bulbs. Its green leaves bear a central white stripe, while flat-topped clusters of white flowers have green-striped petal backs.

A flowering plant endemic to the northern half of the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in Portugal only on the upper Montesinho plateau. Recorded there once in 1989 and rediscovered in 2018, it grows in a mosaic of mountain grassland and hay meadows.

summary: A rhizomatous perennial flowering herb endemic to Portugal, especially its central-western districts. Its flowers have pinkish-flesh petals with a purple-pink upper lip, while the mature seed capsules are very hard.
A flowering plant of the pea family found primarily in the western Mediterranean basin, Calvary clover lives in partnership with a bacterium capable of fixing nitrogen.

Climbing asparagus native from Africa through southern Asia to northern Australia. It has shiny, needle-like green branches and both fibrous and tuberous roots. Minute white flowers appear in July, followed by blackish-purple berries in September.
Orchid native to Assam in India, Yunnan in China, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. Known as Low’s boat orchid, it has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

A boat orchid native to Assam, the Himalaya, south-central China, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet and Vietnam, it grows on trees or rocks and shaded cliffs. Its yellowish-green flowers have brown to reddish-brown lengthwise stripes, with similar red or brown markings on the yellowish lip.

A perennial plant native to Portugal, Spain, France and the Balearic Islands. It has many upright stems, a woody base and dense silvery, felt-like hairs covering its stems, leaves and fruit. Male and female flowers occur on separate plants.

A leguminous shrub native to the Ibero-Maghrebi region, occurring in Spain, Algeria and Morocco. It branches heavily from the base and bears terminal clusters of yellow flowers followed by flattened, silvery hairy pods.

A flowering plant endemic to central and southern parts of the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal only around Monchique and the southwestern Alentejo hills, on rocky slopes and woodland edges. The Portuguese population was assessed as Vulnerable, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants estimated and continuing habitat decline inferred.

An epiphytic bromeliad native to Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, Queen's-tears is often grown as an ornamental.
A short-lived perennial native to Eurasia. It has grey, felted leaves and bright magenta flowers produced successively around July, and readily self-seeds in favourable places.
A moss of unstated native origin, found in Europe and Asia. It forms loose, regularly feathered mats on wet, lime-free rock beside mountain streams and waterfalls, and rarely produces spore capsules.

A conspicuous moss found chiefly in the north Atlantic, golden-head moss has strongholds in western Britain, Ireland and western Norway. It occurs most often in upland acidic grassland, especially near wet flushes.

A thyme-moss found in old-growth boreal forests across North America, Europe and Asia. It forms low lawns in moist but not wet ground, with leaves that curl strongly when dry and spread flat when moist.

An evergreen flowering shrub or tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has narrow leaves and brown, honey-scented spring flowers; cut stems release milky sap that can irritate skin and seriously harm the eyes.

A perennial herb recorded across the Mediterranean region and the Orient, with no explicitly stated native origin. It has thickened roots, woolly-haired stems and large golden-yellow flowers; in Crete it grows in scrub, clay ground and fallow land.

A bulbous plant occurring in mainland Portugal, it grows in traditional dry-farmed olive groves and fallow fields on basic soils. In assessments conducted from 2016 to 2019, it was known there from only two small population clusters near Beja and Beringel and assessed as Critically Endangered, with agricultural intensification the gravest threat.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Its documented biological type is a short-lived plant that survives unfavorable seasons as seed.

An annual herb native in Austria, Germany and Switzerland, with its main distribution around the Mediterranean. It has joined, stem-clasping leaves and rich yellow flowers that open only on sunny mornings.

Portugal's 2020 mainland Red List assessed it as Endangered after its northern coastal range had contracted in recent decades.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Madeira and the Azorean islands of Terceira, Pico, Faial, São Miguel and Santa Maria, it also occurs from southern and western Europe to southwestern Asia. It favours uncultivated ground and flowers from April to July.
A flowering plant represented in continental Portugal by subsp. peixotoanum, which is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Seseli montanum belongs to the carrot family.
Flowering plant endemic to Romania’s Piatra Craiului Mountains. It grows on scree, prefers alkaline substrates and is a symbol of the surrounding massif and national park.
Herbaceous perennial native to France and Spain.

Flowering plant represented in mainland Portugal by three listed subspecies endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Subspecies marizii is described as endemic to mainland Portugal and is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A stonewort native to Europe and northern North America. It chiefly inhabits brackish water but also occurs in a few inland lakes.

Green alga with no stated native origin, widespread across much of Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, and Australia. It is often greyish-green and crusted with calcium carbonate, and can form extensive underwater meadows that shelter aquatic animals.

A small to medium alga with a cosmopolitan distribution. It is transparent, richly branched and lacks a cortex, or outer layer; it was the first member of its class to have its entire nuclear genome sequenced and published.

A stonewort found mainly near the coasts of western and southern Europe, with a wider range from North Africa to northwestern Asia. Its underwater shoots are glossy, translucent and often strongly curved; it lacks spines and rarely becomes encrusted. It typically inhabits acidic moorland waters and cannot tolerate salt.

Its upper branch clusters are rounded and slimy, with a second ring of shorter branches beneath each main cluster. Last recorded in Switzerland in 1920, it is considered regionally extinct there.

summary: An aquatic annual or perennial herb native to Europe, Asia and North America. It has segmented leaves and white, five-petalled flowers with yellow centres, and can photosynthesise underwater.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed along the European and Asian shores of the Mediterranean. In Portugal it inhabited moist coastal meadows, but its last known site was destroyed in the 1990s; it is critically endangered and possibly regionally extinct, though suitable habitat remains insufficiently surveyed.

summary: Plant with no stated native origin, found throughout the Mediterranean Basin. It forms a partnership with the nitrogen-fixing bacterium Sinorhizobium medicae.

A shrub confined to northern Mediterranean coastal Spain and southern France, extending into Italy, and also found in the western Rif, Algeria and Ibiza. Its black, blackberry-like fruit is the largest in its genus but is toxic, and the leaves were traditionally collected for tanning and dyeing.
edibilityNote: The blackberry-like black fruit is toxic; both leaves and fruits contain a convulsant compound.

summary: A rose species with insect-pollinated flowers.

A large shrub or small tree from China, tea-oil camellia has dark green evergreen leaves and fragrant white flowers in mid to late fall. Its seeds can be pressed for a sweetish oil used for seasoning and cooking.
edibilityNote: The seeds are pressed to produce tea seed oil, used as a seasoning and cooking oil.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, small coriander grows in cereal fields, fallows and beneath rain-fed olive groves on basic soils. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Vulnerable, with only three subpopulations then known nationally.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is an upright or ascending, hairless clover with large flower heads surrounded by prominent bracts, found in grassland, fields and hedges in Estremadura, Alentejo and Algarve.

A perennial legume of southern Europe's mountain regions, alpine bird's-foot trefoil sprawls across grassland or rocky surfaces. Its pea-shaped flowers may be yellow, orange or reddish and bloom from May to August.
A grass native to Eurasia, bristle bent forms dense tufts with hairlike leaves. Its yellow-green flower spikelets bear bristles, and it has neither rhizomes nor stolons.

A red alga recorded from Ireland, western Great Britain, Portugal and the Mediterranean. Its short, flat fronds rise from a creeping, branched holdfast and branch once or twice, with cylindrical growths at their tips.

A biennial herb of the Mediterranean region, also recorded across parts of Europe, western Asia and Africa. Its leaves change from heart-shaped or divided lower leaves to narrow-segmented upper leaves. It bears white flowers in many-rayed clusters and small, outwardly hairy fruits.
edibilityNote: Its seeds are listed for food use and as a spice or aromatic crop under “anise seeds.”

summary: An autumn-flowering plant found from Portugal and Morocco east to Turkey and the Caucasus, as well as in Great Britain. Though classified as one species, it is a complex of outwardly indistinguishable forms with different chromosome complements.

A perennial bunch grass native to Eurasia, China and India, rough reedgrass grows in tufts with short underground stems. It has upright stems, rough narrow leaves and open, lance-shaped flower clusters.

Perennial bulb-forming herb occurring in the northeastern Mediterranean, with no explicitly stated native origin. It bears daughter bulbs and flowers from March to April in habitats including scrub, fallow ground and olive groves.

A perennial plant from Syria, Lebanon, the Palestine region, the eastern Mediterranean and southern Europe. It has a ground-hugging rosette of deeply divided leaves, bright pink flowers nearly year-round and long-beaked fruits.

Herbaceous perennial flowering plant native to the eastern Mediterranean. It has wine-red flowers with white, red-spotted lower lips and evergreen, lightly hairy leaves that produce no scent when crushed.
edibilityNote: In Jordanian and Palestinian cuisine, the leaves are stuffed with meat and rice and cooked with lamb riblets.

summary: A perennial sedge native to tropical parts of the Americas, shortleaf spikesedge has spreading underground stems and several upright shoots. It produces tiny clusters of spikelets and is sometimes a weed in wet cultivated ground and irrigation ditches.
A banyan fig found from South and southern China through Indo-China and Peninsular Malaysia to parts of Malesia, including Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, Sulawesi and Maluku.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There it grows in dry annual meadows, pastures and path edges, particularly on siliceous and often sandy soils.

summary: An evergreen tree native to South Africa.

A flowering plant native to Tunisia, Sardinia, Corsica, Sicily, Italy, Albania, Greece, the eastern Aegean Islands, Crete, Cyprus and Turkey, Malva cretica has been introduced to France. A possible subspecies may occur in Spain.
A flowering plant native to the shores of the western and central Mediterranean, it is known as tree mallow or sea mallow.
Annual herb native to central Europe, the Mediterranean and the Caucasus. It grows upright without support and has simple, broad leaves.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on coastal dunes and other seaside sands; reports that its basal leaves narrow abruptly into clear stalks and its stem leaves are spoon-shaped need confirmation.
A tree native to Guangdong and Hainan in China, Taiwan and Vietnam. Its leaves are used in Taiwanese folk medicine as an expectorant.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in cool, damp meadows and along rivers, particularly at the edges of riverside woodland.
A flowering plant introduced to mainland Portugal; its native origin is not supplied. It grows on sunny limestone slopes, in rock crevices and on walls.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced to Madeira. It grows in wet meadows, sometimes where the ground is somewhat salty.

Flowering plant of unspecified native origin, introduced in parts of mainland Portugal. It grows semi-prostrate to upright but tends to flatten when grazed. It flowers from May to June, producing blooms attractive to bees.

A perennial flowering herb native to mainland Portugal, it grows prostrate without rooting along its stems. It has deeply pink flowers and large pink fruiting heads, and occurs in scrub, woods and shady places.

A poisonous evergreen shrub native to Monos Island, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela and its Antilles, Guyana, Brazil, and northwest Argentina. It is commonly cultivated as an ornamental and used in ayahuasca and other potions.
Orchid native to the Mediterranean region from Portugal and Morocco east to Syria.

Flowering plant native to northwestern Africa, nearly all of Europe, the Caucasus, the Middle East and Central Asia. It resembles the dog rose but has downier leaves, especially on their undersides; its cultivar ‘Laxa’ is widely used in Europe as garden-rose rootstock.

Wild onion native to Spain, France, Italy, Morocco and Tunisia. It bears numerous small white or pink flowers and an egg-shaped bulb, often surrounded by bulblets; its strongly aromatic bulbs and foliage are cultivated for food.
edibilityNote: The potently aromatic bulbs and foliage are widely cultivated for eating.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in pastures and scrub clearings on either basic or acidic soils; reports of unusually broad, roughly rectangular fruit valves with an indented tip need confirmation.
An annual Mediterranean herb with a slender, fleshy taproot. It produces bluish-violet flower heads, and its leaves are edible.
edibilityNote: The leaves are edible.

summary: An annual herb native to the Mediterranean, western Europe, the Middle East as far as Iran, and North Africa, slender salsify grows in dry disturbed ground, vineyards, roadsides and meadows. Its pink-to-violet flower heads rise on hollow stalks swollen beneath them, and it produces two differently formed kinds of seed-bearing fruit.

A perennial herb found mainly in southern and central Europe, three-leaved anemone grows in hardwood forests and rocky places. It has three-part, toothed leaves and usually single white flowers, though pale pink or blue forms occur. Its shallow whitish underground stems can produce dense colonies.

A perennial, winter-deciduous caper found in parts of Spain, North Africa, the Middle East, Turkey and Crete. Its upright branches resprout in spring and can form a thick trunk, and its elongated fruit contains yellow pulp.

Woolly annual plant native to the Mediterranean region. It produces early flower heads beneath its basal leaf rosette and later yellow heads on upright stems. Its five seed types differ in size, position, dispersal and whether germination is immediate or delayed.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There it is confined to the central Algarve Barrocal, growing in dry fallows, pastures and traditional rain-fed orchards, especially on red clay over limestone.

summary: An annual herb native from the Canary Islands across the Mediterranean region and neighboring areas to Iran, Cretanweed has variably hairy or bristly growth. Most leaves cluster around the base and resemble dandelion leaves, while its stalks carry single yellow flower heads or flat-topped groups of heads.
A flowering plant in the daisy family, native to mainland Portugal.

An annual herb found throughout the Mediterranean, though absent from most smaller islands and from Corsica, Sardinia and Sicily. It is densely covered with sticky yellowish hairs and has lemon-yellow flowers; its leaves change from three leaflets low on the plant to one higher up.

summary: An annual grass found in southern Europe, North Africa, southwestern Asia and Madeira. Its slender stems commonly trail before rising, and its thin flower spikes grow in coastal salt marshes and other salty ground.
A flowering herb whose subspecies Scandix australis subsp. australis is native to mainland Portugal. The species has awl-shaped, hairy seeds, radiating flowers and smooth stems.

A small herb native from the Mediterranean region east to Afghanistan. Whitish hairs cover its leaves and stems, and its pink or purple flowers form small, compact heads.

summary: Annual herb with a wide circum-Mediterranean distribution; no explicitly native origin is stated. It has simple broad leaves, and in mainland Portugal it occurs only in the Algarve on stabilized dunes and consolidated coastal sands.

summary: An annual herb with no native origin supplied, Valantia hispida is a very small, self-supporting plant. It has simple, broad leaves.

Perennial mint-family herb of unstated native origin, lesser calamint commonly grows around the Mediterranean, North Africa and parts of Central Asia. Its fragrant, grey-green leaves resemble oregano and smell of pennyroyal, while its flowers are lavender-pink. It is used as a culinary herb in Italian and Corsican cooking, including Roman-style artichokes and a southern Italian goat cheese.
edibilityNote: Used as a culinary herb in Italian and Corsican food, including Roman-style artichokes and southern Italian goat cheese.

summary: A flowering plant native to Spain, including the Balearic Islands, France, including Corsica, and Italy, it has traditionally been used to treat haemorrhoids.

Orchid endemic to Portugal and western Spain. In mainland Portugal it occurs very sparsely in moist meadows on sandy or siliceous soils and was assessed as Endangered following habitat and population declines.

summary: A medium-sized orchid restricted to Java and the Lesser Sunda Islands. Its flower clusters carry cream-white to mauve blooms marked with many brownish-purple spots, gently wavy edges and a three-lobed lip.
An epiphytic orchid from the cool, moist eastern Himalayas and Vietnam, it blooms around the spring snowmelt. Its fragrant flowers have snow-white petals and a yellow-marked lip.

An epiphytic orchid endemic to Vietnam, it grows on trees in montane rainforests and on plateaus. Its showy white flowers have numerous small orange appendages on the lip and appear from spring into early summer.
A flowering plant native to southeastern Brazil, from Espírito Santo to Rio Grande do Sul.
An orchid found in Assam, southern China and parts of Myanmar. Its populations face pressure from habitat degradation and collection for the plant trade.

An orchid native to the Malay Peninsula, Thailand, Myanmar and Borneo at low elevations. Its few very large, hanging flowers are pale yellow to cream with red stripes or spots, and have exceptionally long side sepals.

An orchid native to the Himalayas and the mountains of northern Indochina, Dendrobium thyrsiflorum has two recognized varieties. The variety minutiflorum is recorded from Laos, while the typical variety covers most of the species’ range.

Perennial climbing ivy native from Afghanistan through the Himalayas and southern China to mainland Southeast Asia. It has glossy evergreen leaves and orange-to-red fruits, and all parts are poisonous.
edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; ingestion can cause gastrointestinal and nervous-system disturbances.

summary: An annual herb of unstated native origin, it has broad compound leaves and a self-supporting form. It produces chemicals that suppress the growth of nearby plants.

A freshwater microscopic green alga with a cosmopolitan distribution, Pseudopediastrum boryanum occurs most commonly in nutrient-rich waters, but also in brackish water and some mountain water bodies. Its colonies form flat, star-like discs, while its decay-resistant cell walls are often preserved in lake sediments.

Perennial flowering herb native to Madeira and the Salvage Islands. It usually forms dense mats, has leaves divided into five leaflets, and bears flowers that generally open orange before turning reddish-brown after fertilization.
Annual flowering plant native to southwestern Europe and North Africa. It bears dense, spherical clusters of pale blue flowers, followed by showy fruits with striped, fan-like papery bracts.
A flowering plant native to a range extending from Europe to the Russian Far East and Iran.

A perennial herb growing in southern and central Europe and western and central Asia, it inhabits warm grasslands, including dry limestone sites. It has many stems, scattered leaves and white latex, with small flowers arranged in complex umbrella-like clusters.

summary: A perennial flowering plant indigenous to southeastern Africa. Though commonly called a fern, it is an asparagus with fine, bushy stems and needle-like leaves; its small red fruits turn black as they mature.
edibilityNote: It is reported to have little or no nutritional value to people, but its edibility is not explicitly established.

summary: A dense deciduous shrub native to the Korean Peninsula and nearby parts of Northeast China, Japan and the Russian Far East. Its late-spring to early-summer flowers are white to pink, often with small red spots on the upper petals. Azaleas are poisonous and cannot be eaten.
edibilityNote: Azaleas are described as poisonous and not edible.

summary: An annual herb whose native origin is not supplied, it has yellow flowers in small clusters and slightly curved pods divided into one-seeded sections. In Portugal it occurs near the coast in fields, roadsides and other disturbed places on sandy or limestone ground.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In the 2020 Portuguese assessment, its occurrence on Arrábida's sea cliffs was the only mainland European record; only five individuals were then known, and it was assessed as Endangered.

summary: An annual herb endemic to the Mediterranean region, it grows in open, stony places, especially on limestone or gypsum. Its dense flower cluster has purple glands, while its grey seeds bear six lengthwise grooves; it flowers and fruits in March.

A perennial tufted grass with a paleotropical distribution reaching the Mediterranean and southwestern Asia, it favors dry, sunny grasslands, scrub openings and rocky ground. Its unbranched stems end in paired cylindrical flower spikes with conspicuously long bristles.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to Macaronesia, central Europe, the Mediterranean region, and central and southwestern Asia, and naturalized in America. Its pale blue-violet flowers form dense clusters, and its persistent calyx has six hooked teeth.

A herbaceous grass native from the Mediterranean region to western Asia. This uncommon plant grows in temporarily waterlogged grassland, sandy banks and roadsides, with erect ridged stems and long, spike-like flowering branches.

A small annual flowering herb native to mainland Portugal, it grows in scrub clearings and damp grassland on stony limestone ground. There, it is known only from scattered sites in the Algarve’s Barrocal and is assessed as Vulnerable.

summary: A tree found from Costa Rica to Bolivia, it has aromatic glands on its leaves and pleasantly scented wax granules on its fruits. The fruit wax is used for candles, varnishes and polishes.

An annual herb of the central and eastern Mediterranean coastline, commonly growing in uncultivated places near the sea. Its leaves divide into fan-shaped segments, and its pinkish-white flowers have purple tips. It flowers from February to April.
A flowering plant native to mainland China, where its fertile form has particular cultural significance.
A tall, erect herb widespread across most of Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. It bears branching clusters of small white flowers.
A bulbous flowering plant native to Iran, Turkey and Turkmenistan. It produces large, showy clusters of silvery-pink, star-shaped flowers in early summer, followed by attractive fruiting clusters.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in somewhat disturbed fallows and annual pastures on siliceous, often sandy soils.
A flowering plant, Herniaria scabrida has listed varieties found in mainland Portugal and described as native only to the Iberian Peninsula.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is present there but is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, including mainland Portugal.

A perennial herb native to western Europe's sub-Atlantic region. It has blue-green leaves that may be dark-spotted, with dense soft white hairs along their margins and undersides, and bears yellow flower heads from late spring into summer.

sources.title: Hieracium glaucinum Jord.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Annual herb found in pinewoods and heathlands of the western and northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It has spoon-shaped, serrated basal leaves and yellow, sunflower-like flower heads from April to August.
A perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on rocky slopes, scree and rock crevices, usually on siliceous stone, and has mostly opposite hairy leaves with solitary flower heads.

summary: A perennial grass native to Portugal, Spain and Morocco. It has linear blue-green leaves and flowers arranged in branching clusters.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

An annual grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows on temporarily wet ledges and sandy, stony or rocky soils. It has short, upright hollow stems, very hairy narrow leaves and small compressed flower clusters.
An annual grass whose native origin is not stated in the supplied sources. In Portugal it grows in open scrub on poor, dry soils.
Flowering member of the mint family endemic to central and northern Portugal. It grows on granite-based ground beside paths and roads, on damp slopes and pastures, and along cultivated field edges.

A shrub or dwarf shrub endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits mountain thorn scrub, especially on granite and quartzite exposed to strong, cold winter winds, and its flowers release an intense honey scent.

A woody, thorny shrub endemic to the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. Its rigid grooved stems end in spines, while yellow flowers appear along older branches in spring; it grows mainly in scrub on siliceous ground.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Armeria transmontana occurs in mainland Portugal. It is not protected by Portuguese or European Union legislation.

A low-growing rose-family plant endemic to the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It has arching wine-red prickly shoots, five-part leaves and white or pale-pink flowers, and occurs in woodland openings, forest edges and roadsides, mainly on siliceous soils.

summary: A low-growing rose-family plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Its trailing reddish-brown prickly shoots bear numerous hairs and dark reddish glands; the leaves usually have three parts with grey-green woolly undersides, and the flowers are white or pale pink.

summary: Small shrub native to Haiti and the Dominican Republic. It has large leaves often tinted red or maroon beneath, and long, drooping tubular flowers in red-orange or red-purple with protruding stamens.

A long-lived perennial herb native to continental Eurasian cliffs and slopes, especially on limestone, white swallow-wort has upright stems with white five-petalled flowers. Its fruits contain many seeds topped with tufts of white hairs. The plant is poisonous.
edibilityNote: The plant is described as poisonous; no qualified edible use is documented.

summary: Evergreen flowering shrub or tree native to New Caledonia. Its toothed leaves have several thin leaflets, changing from coppery red to dark green, while pale green autumn flowers are followed by black fruit.
A small tree or multi-stemmed mallee endemic to Western Australia. It has smooth, variously coloured bark that sheds in ribbons and lemon-yellow flowers appearing from late winter to late spring.

Erect herb with no explicitly stated native origin, widespread across most of Europe and extending into Morocco, the Caucasus and southwestern Asia. It has almost round leaves in whorls of four and green fruits covered with long hooked hairs.

An evergreen flowering shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and Mexico, Texas mountain laurel bears intensely fragrant purple flowers that smell like grape soda. Its pods contain orange or red seeds that are extremely toxic if swallowed.
edibilityNote: The seeds are extremely toxic; consuming a single seed can kill an adult.

summary: An orchid found from the Florida Everglades through the Caribbean, Mexico and Central America to northern Brazil.

An annual or biennial flowering herb native to western Europe, North Africa and the Mediterranean Basin, Cretan mallow has hairy stems, lobed leaves and small pink or light-purple flowers. Its leaf blades track the sun during the day and turn to face sunrise.
An orchid herb native to coastal and Andean Ecuador and surrounding countries, it ranges from Costa Rica to Ecuador.

A short-lived evergreen perennial native to South Africa, Bacopa is found predominantly along the country’s southern coast. It grows as an annual in colder climates and requires full sun to flower profusely.

A perennial flowering plant native to the Rocky Mountains of the western United States, blue columbine grows from foothills to above the timberline. Its large, scented flowers usually combine white or cream petals with blue sepals and have five long, nearly straight spurs. Bumblebees and hawkmoths are its main pollinators.

Herbaceous perennial native to subtropical Sichuan in southern China. Its trunklike false stems support a crown of large green leaves, while its yellow-green fruits are inedible, with sparse white pulp and many black seeds.
edibilityNote: The yellow-green fruits are inedible, containing little white pulp and many black seeds.

summary: Flowering tree native to China, the Korean Peninsula, Japan and the Russian Far East. It is used as a street tree within its native range but is susceptible to damage from late frosts.

A shrub or small-to-medium tree native to southern Africa, from southern Angola east to Mozambique and south to South Africa. It is readily recognised by its exceptionally long paired white thorns and coffee-coloured bark.
edibilityNote: Gum from cracks in the bark was used to make sweets and formerly had economic importance as Cape Gum.

summary: Herbaceous perennial or subshrub native to the Atlantic coasts of northern Europe. It has strongly aromatic, pale grey-green foliage covered in dense white cottony hairs and grows mainly in dry coastal places with saline soils.

Flowering plant endemic to South Africa and recorded in the Hottentots Holland Nature Reserve. It has finely divided leaves and white-to-pink flowers that appear from July to October in its native range, and it is grown for cut flowers and as an ornamental.

A shrub or medium-sized tree native to parts of eastern and central Africa, the African milkbush has fleshy young stems and green leaves that may be reddish underneath. Wounds release poisonous white latex, while cultivated forms can have purple-red foliage.
Annual flowering plant whose native origin is not supplied. The Zuni grind its seeds with cornmeal, form the mixture into cakes and steam them for food.
edibilityNote: The Zuni traditionally grind the seeds with cornmeal, make them into cakes and steam them.

summary: A herbaceous perennial typical of most of the Alps and Italy’s Apennines, it grows in meadows, uncultivated fields and mountain pastures. Its basal leaves have a greyish waxy coating, and its white funnel-shaped flowers appear from late April through June.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and recorded from mainland Portugal.

A woody-stemmed Mediterranean herb found mainly in coastal habitats, though occasionally inland on sandy ground and road cuttings. It has numerous dense, narrow, awl-shaped leaves, while its flowers form relatively loose spikes in spring and summer.

Bulbous perennial endemic to Morocco and Portugal, although Moroccan plants have often been confused with a distinct species. This dwarf bluebell has long, narrow leaves and blue, violet or white bell- or star-shaped flowers in spring. It grows in damp, often sandy open ground near sea level.
A tulip native to Central Asia and Iran. It has large, single bowl-shaped flowers in red, yellow or white and distinctive green leaves patterned with purple-maroon spots and stripes.

Rhizomatous perennial iris native to western China. Its glossy leaves grow atop bamboo-like stems, and its white to pale blue flowers have orange-yellow crests and purple dots. Most parts, particularly the rhizomes and leaves, are poisonous if swallowed and may cause stomach pain and vomiting.
edibilityNote: Most parts are poisonous; ingested rhizomes and leaves may cause stomach pain and vomiting.

summary: A flowering plant from northern Myanmar, Yunnan in China, South Korea and northern Kyushu in Japan, the Korean azalea has a notably disjunct distribution. It is recommended for hedges and has above-average resistance to the root rot that often affects azaleas.
A bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil. Several cultivars are grown as ornamental plants.
An ornamental plant endemic to eastern Brazil, where it is known from Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro states. It is widely cultivated.
An evergreen dwarf shrub native to southern Spain, woolly lavender has striking silver, woolly leaves and deep violet-purple flower spikes with a familiar lavender scent.

A flowering shrub native to southern Madeira and Lanzarote in the Canary Islands. Its deeply divided leaves are covered in fine white hairs, giving it a downy appearance, and deep violet flower spikes bloom from late spring into summer.
A small herb whose native origin is not explicitly specified, found across parts of Asia including the eastern Himalayas. It grows in moist, shaded places, often beside streams.

A flowering plant endemic to the Azores, restricted to Corvo and Flores. It inhabits very humid rocky slopes, waterfall surroundings and lake margins, and was rediscovered in 1999 after going unobserved since 1938.
Valentine's sunflower is a plant native to Europe, with some occurrences in Morocco and Algeria. Most are found in Spain.
A flowering plant endemic to central and northern Portugal, it grows along woodland and hedge edges on ultrabasic, schist or limestone soils.

An annual daisy native to North Africa and southern Europe. It has finely divided, somewhat fleshy leaves and white outer flowers surrounding yellow central florets, and grows in grasslands, fields and roadsides on clay or marl soils.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across the western Mediterranean. In Portugal it occurs only sporadically in Trás-os-Montes, on rocky outcrops and in holm-oak clearings. Portugal’s 2020 Red List assessed it as Vulnerable, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants estimated nationally.

A flowering plant of unspecified native origin, recorded across Europe and temperate Asia.

summary: Rock-growing bromeliad endemic to Brazil. This giant grows on rocky slopes in Rio de Janeiro’s Serra dos Órgãos and can take up to 40 years to produce its imposing red flower cluster. Its leaf tank can hold substantial rainwater.
A flowering plant species native to mainland Portugal.

An arable flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Linaria hirta occurs exclusively in extensive rain-fed farmland such as traditional olive groves, cereal fields and fallows. In mainland Portugal it was assessed as Vulnerable, with agricultural intensification identified as its main threat.

summary: A flowering plant of unspecified native origin, introduced to mainland Portugal. There it is naturalised in wall cracks, old walls and rocky places, flowers throughout the year, and has a recorded range of less than one square kilometre.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A plant endemic to Kenya, tiger-tooth aloe is restricted to a small rocky mountainous area in the southwest near Tanzania. It is extremely rare in the wild but common in cultivation. Short, straight triangular leaves grow densely along its stems, and it has twice the usual chromosome set reported for many aloes.

A biennial herb of unstated native origin, found in the western Mediterranean from southern Italy and Sicily through the Iberian Peninsula to North Africa. It has a persistent grey-white or yellow-green woolly covering and yellow flowers whose purple basal marks form a ring around the throat.

A short-lived perennial herb endemic to the Azores, it occurs on Pico, São Jorge and Terceira and is presumed extinct on Faial. It has large, showy white flowers tinged purple or lilac, with yellow markings. As a root hemiparasite, it probably exploits neighbouring plants’ roots.

A herbaceous plant endemic to the western islands of the Azores, it is protected under the Bern Convention and Habitats Directive. It is closely related to Euphrasia grandiflora, which is endemic to the archipelago’s central islands.

A flowering plant native to the western half of the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in wet depressions and moisture-loving scrub on peat or waterlogged sandy soils, mainly in scattered coastal populations, and is Near Threatened in mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. In Portugal it grows in grassy places beneath holm-oak, cork-oak and wild-olive woodland, along woodland edges or on rocky outcrops.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant present in Portugal; its subsp. lobelioides is native and endemic to Macaronesia and occurs in Madeira.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant whose variety sabularia is endemic to mainland Portugal. That variety is protected under Portuguese or European legislation.

Annual flowering herb whose native origin is not supplied at species level; its subsp. chrysanthemoides is native to mainland Portugal. It bears solitary yellow flower heads and inhabits grassland, cropland, disturbed ground, roadsides and earthy slopes, preferring basic soils.

summary: A perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and northwest Africa. Its rose-purple flower heads rise above variable leaves whose veins are covered on both sides with distinctive white wool.

summary: A flowering plant species reported from Portugal.

An annual herb native to Europe and parts of Asia and northern Africa. Its upright stem is often red or red-streaked, while its toothed leaves have smooth upper surfaces and powdery undersides. Powdery clusters of spherical buds remain closed as the fruit develops.
edibilityNote: Seeds are edible; shoots, stalks and leaves can be eaten as greens, historically used like spinach.

summary: Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but introduced in the Azores. In Portugal it grows in crop fields, fallow land, pastures and dry meadows, often on stony ground.

An annual herb native to North Africa and western Mediterranean Europe. Its flowers are white to pale pink, with dark purple tips only on the inner petals; it has become invasive in parts of South America where introduced.
Perennial subshrub native to the Canary Islands and Madeira, it belongs to the nettle family and grows in subtropical regions. It has also been introduced to the Azores.

Annual flowering plant endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. It occupies stony pasture, scrub clearings and rocky slopes, including altered soils in mining areas; in mainland Portugal it is assessed as Near Threatened amid continuing habitat and population declines.

Mediterranean flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In the western Algarve it inhabits rock fissures, scree and limestone coastal cliffs. A 2020 mainland assessment classified Portugal's declining population as Critically Endangered, with fewer than 250 mature plants concentrated in one subpopulation.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced to the Azores and Madeira. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Union legislation.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Diplotaxis virgata subsp. virgata is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

An annual herb in the mustard family, it forms a basal leaf rosette and flowering stems that may have leaves or be leafless. In western Europe it blooms from June through October, while elsewhere in its range flowering may extend for up to eight months.
A flowering plant in the cabbage family with several varieties native to mainland Portugal, including laevigata, valentina and variegata.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. In Portugal it grows along roadsides and in farmland and fallow ground, especially on disturbed soils.

sources.title: Silene nocturna L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant in the carnation family, native in countries from the Mediterranean to northern Somalia and Pakistan. It is listed as invasive in Australia and France, occurring particularly in drier parts of southeastern Australia.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. In Portugal it grows on dunes, pastures and dry meadows with sandy soils, usually near the coast but also on inland sands.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in dry places with basic soils, including pastures, scrub clearings, fallow or cultivated fields and roadsides.

Tillandsia species native to Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. Its recognised varieties and subspecies have more restricted ranges within Bolivia and Argentina, while the typical subspecies occupies most of the species’ range.

An annual legume whose wild forms are native to Anatolia, northern Iraq and the Anti-Lebanon Mountains of Syria and Lebanon. Its split grain resembles red lentils, but the bitter seeds require leaching through several changes of boiling water before human consumption; historically, they were eaten mainly by poor people or during famine.
edibilityNote: Seeds require repeated changes of boiling water to remove bitterness; historically they were eaten mainly by poor people or during famine.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits dry, sunny grasslands and fallow fields with stony soils and sometimes occurs among crops.
A bedstraw species native to the Mediterranean Basin from Portugal and Morocco east to Turkey and Palestine, it is distinguished by numerous wart-like bumps on its mature fruit.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Its narrow leaves are deeply lobed, while its flower stalks often lie along the ground and swell beneath the flower head. It grows chiefly in annual grassland, scrub clearings and soil-filled hollows on stony limestone.

sources.title: Hyoseris scabra L.
sources.attribution: Kilian N (2024). Cichorieae Systematics Portal. Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/gzcrwf accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An annual herb found in southern Europe, northwest Africa, the Caucasus and the Middle East, edible star-hawkbit typically grows in Mediterranean scrub and forest. Its flowers are yellow and may host the fungus Puccinia rhagadioli.

An annual herb found in the northeastern Mediterranean and the Middle East, from Albania and Greece to Iraq and Iran. It has deeply divided leaves, a leafy stem that becomes nearly hairless above, and spindle-shaped, unwinged fruits.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There, it occurs only at scattered sites between Cape Espichel and the western Algarve. It grows on coastal cliffs with very thin, usually sandy but sometimes clay soils.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium echioides
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Flowering subshrub native to coastal Mediterranean and Red Sea areas and parts of the Middle East and central Asia. It grows in salty soils and has succulent jointed stems that yellow with age, with stubby bluish-green leaves clasping each joint.

A woody plant native to mainland Portugal, Madeira and the Azores, sea knotgrass is usually prostrate, with thick, twisted stems and lance-shaped leaves. A 1913 Portuguese flora describes it as frequent on coastal sands and present in flower almost all year.

A spreading or trailing succulent herb native to South Africa’s KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga provinces and to Eswatini. Its succulent stems are four-angled, and the small leaves may occasionally have purplish undersides with red gland dots; flowers are white or pale mauve.
A wild onion native to Algeria and Morocco.

sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). English Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/c3kkgh accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Wild onion native to the Mediterranean region and Middle East, from Portugal and Algeria to Iran. It has a single egg-shaped bulb, long fleshy leaves, and white or pale-purple bell-shaped flowers, some nodding and others upright in the same cluster.
An arrowgrass species native to the Maltese Islands, it favors rainwater pools on karst limestone in garigue and on valley sides. It blooms from March to April and has inconspicuous flowers.
A low-growing flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It favors dry slopes, rock cracks and stony soils, usually on silica-rich ground, but also occurs in coastal sandy soils.

Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it occurs mainly in Trás-os-Montes and Beira Alta, with a small residual presence in Beira Litoral, growing on schist slopes and banks. A 2016–2019 mainland Portuguese assessment classified it as Vulnerable, estimating fewer than 1,000 mature plants nationally despite uncertainty about population size.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in openings among scrub and in rock fissures, usually on limestone and more rarely on quartzite.

summary: Annual flowering herb native to the Mediterranean and Eastern Europe. It grows in gravelly soil, rocky slopes and dry grassland, flowering from March to early summer.
A flowering plant native to the Madeira Archipelago. It occurs on Porto Santo but not on Madeira, the Selvagens or the Desertas.
A flowering plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula and present in continental Portugal. It belongs to the Resedaceae family.
A deciduous maple tree found in southeastern Europe and western Asia. Its usually five-lobed leaves are dark above and waxy, paler green beneath; greenish-yellow flowers open in early spring.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and belonging to the carnation family.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows and pastures on sandy soil.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Silene inaperta subsp. inaperta is native to mainland Portugal and Madeira.

A low-growing flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and associated particularly with its northwest. It grows on granite cliffs, rocky cracks, soil-covered ledges and stony slopes, preferring shaded places.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula that grows in stony soils over ultrabasic rock. In mainland Portugal it occurs only in Bragança-Vinhais; a 2020 assessment rated it Vulnerable, although national population estimates were inconsistent.

summary: A flowering plant with two varieties described as endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Variety duriensis is present in mainland Portugal, while the presence there of variety penyalarensis is doubtful.
An annual flowering plant native to continental Portugal. It grows in dry, open grassland, uncultivated ground and disturbed places, often on clay-rich soils.

A perennial flowering plant reported from Spain and North Africa; Portuguese records formerly assigned to it are now considered Daucus junceus. It occurs in rocky, often shaded clearings, slopes and roadsides, sometimes beside rivers.
A low evergreen shrub of northern regions, growing on peaty soils and in moss and lichen tundra. Clusters of small white flowers give off a strong scent that attracts pollinating insects.
edibilityNote: Historically used in medieval beer brewing; all parts contain poisonous compounds, so this record does not establish safe consumption.

summary: A perennial flowering plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in scrub clearings and grasslands, often in shade, on either limestone or silica-rich ground.
An annual flowering plant native to continental Portugal. It inhabits temporary pools and damp hollows that are periodically flooded, on silica-rich ground.

summary: A flowering herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in wet meadows on siliceous ground, usually in mountain areas. Mainland Portugal’s 2016–2019 assessment classified it as Vulnerable and identified only four locations there.

summary: A creeping moss found mainly on lime-free rocks and sometimes on trees. It branches like a small tree; when dry, its leaves overlap like roof tiles and curve to one side, but when damp they stand slightly away from the stem.

A shrub endemic to eastern Australia, occurring in northern New South Wales and south-eastern Queensland. Its young leaves and shoots are hairy, and its yellow flowers have rolled-back tips that form a cross when viewed end-on. Green fruits follow flowering from December to February.

A woody flowering plant native to continental Portugal and found mainly in central Europe, though its wider distribution is not fully known. Its leaflets have toothed edges and glands along the central veins, while the leaf stalks are densely glandular.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Flowering plant with no stated native origin. It is recorded in mainland Portugal and described as introduced in the regions referenced by the source.
A flowering plant native to continental Portugal. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant whose subspecies rotundifolium is documented as native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant endemic to the western Iberian Peninsula, living in rush beds and waterlogged meadows. In mainland Portugal it had not been observed since the early 1990s despite targeted surveys, so a 2020 assessment considered it Critically Endangered and potentially regionally extinct, while allowing that hidden populations might survive.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced to the Madeira archipelago.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A cactus-like flowering shrub native to South Africa, the African milk barrel has blue-green, heavily ridged, spiny stems and solitary green flowers in summer. When damaged, it releases toxic white sap that irritates skin and eyes.

An upright, woody perennial native to South Africa, butterfly pelargonium has softly hairy side shoots and heart-shaped leaves. Its pale pink to crimson flowers have two large upper petals marked with a dark violet blotch and three smaller lower petals. It grows along forest edges and in partly shaded places near streams in the southern Western and Eastern Cape.

A perennial herb with no stated native origin, known exclusively from five Spanish provinces. Its grey-green, woolly leaves have toothed divisions, while its pink or purple flowers appear in late spring and summer.
Terrestrial plant native to Argentina and Bolivia. It can form large, dense mats of leaves and is also grown elsewhere as a potted houseplant or ground cover.
A lupine of unspecified native origin, sand lupine is recorded from parts of North Africa and southern Europe, including Mediterranean islands.
Flowering plant in the daisy family, with its subspecies C. limbata subsp. lusitana endemic to mainland Portugal and its variety C. limbata var. limbata native there.
A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A flowering plant native to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. It grows in loose, slightly moist but unflooded sand, usually near temporary ponds; in Portugal it occurs in only four concentrated subpopulations and was assessed as Vulnerable.

summary: A perennial herb native to Turkey and endemic to the Çatalca Peninsula. It is threatened by habitat loss.
Bulbous perennial endemic to South Africa’s Cape Province. Its winter or spring flower clusters may be orange, red, yellow or rarely white, often with a green or brown centre.
edibilityNote: Reported to be toxic if ingested; its leaves also cause irritation.

summary: A perennial herb occurring from North Africa and southern Europe east to Turkmenistan, it has low, trailing stems and spreads locally through underground stems, often forming small cloned patches. Soft, silky hairs cover both sides of its narrow leaves, giving the plant a distinctive silver appearance.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Evergreen oak endemic to Cyprus and confined to the Troodos Mountains. It is a much-branched shrub or small tree, remembered for glossy dark-green leaves with golden or brownish undersides and acorns with strongly backward-curving cup scales.
An annual grass native to Mediterranean Basin countries in North Africa, southern Europe, and western Asia, extending east to Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Pakistan.

A bromeliad endemic to southeastern Brazil, growing in humid, shaded Atlantic Forest at low altitudes. Its green leaves have irregular dark cross-bands and curved-back tips, and it typically produces branching yellow, cream or white flowers in spring.
A perennial moss of unstated native origin, observed in western North America. It forms small, erect green to brownish-green tufts in scattered colonies on rocky outcrops and shallow-soil grasslands.

An annual aquatic herb native to Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Spain, Italy and Portugal. In mainland Portugal, it is known only from an Algarve collection made in the 1980s and was assessed as Critically Endangered, possibly regionally extinct, although it may persist or have escaped detection.

summary: Perennial shrub or tree native to Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

A clumping perennial grass native to Eurasia, it produces sturdy upright stems topped by branched clusters of spikelets. Elsewhere it occurs as an introduced plant and casual weed of disturbed ground.
A plant native to Brazil and Uruguay.

Succulent native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, Coast Oxtongue forms rosettes of exceptionally long, curved, sharply pointed green leaves densely banded with tiny white spots. Pink flowers appear on a tall, flat-topped, branching stalk between September and December.
Succulent native to South Africa’s Cape Provinces and KwaZulu-Natal. It has long, unbranched, rambling stems and a long flower cluster bearing many tiny cream flowers between November and April.

A succulent shrub native to Namibia and the Cape Provinces of South Africa, it grows into a rounded, heavily branched plant. Its powdery gray-green leaves are fused in opposite pairs, have reddish edges, and may turn reddish in intense sunlight.

A perennial rosette plant occurring in South Africa’s Western Cape, Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal, usually in the shade of thickets. It spreads by long arching shoots into dense groups, with green leaves that are purple underneath and small white flowers appearing from winter to midsummer.

A flowering plant native to South Africa’s Western and Northern Cape Provinces. Its narrow leaves curl into spirals and may have non-sticky glandular hairs at their tips. Nodding green flowers have pale yellow edges and a sweet, vanilla-like scent.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and belonging to the carrot family.

Tuberous flowering plant native to montane cloud forests on the eastern Andes of Bolivia and Argentina. Its stems rise from a tuberous base and carry paired or tripled bright orange-pink flowers with four pointed segments.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Rubus galloecicus belongs to the rose family and occurs in mainland Portugal.

Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and, within Iberia, recorded only in central and northern Portugal. It usually occurs in small groups along woodland edges, clearings, field hedges and paths; its population and distribution are uncertain because it may be confused with Rubus radula. It was assessed as Vulnerable in mainland Portugal as a precaution.

summary: A perennial flowering herb or small shrub endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in rocky crevices and stony grassland, with greenish-yellow flowers that are often reddish.

sources.attribution: F. Munoz Garmendia, C. Navarro, S. Castroviejo, plazi (1999). Flora Iberica / Vol. VI: Rosaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/7jx4n7 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It has reddish, arching or trailing canes bearing numerous prickles and yellowish stalked glands, plus white flowers and leaves with grey-green, felted undersides.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Its mostly hairless green or reddish canes have prickles with conspicuously red bases, while the five-part leaves have wavy edges and soft, grey-white undersides. The flowers have large white petals.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It has wine-red, arching or trailing canes crowded with hairs and prickles, and five-part leaves with grey, felted undersides. Its flowers are white or pale pink.

summary: A bramble from southern and central Europe and southwestern Asia. It is a rare, limited-range member of a group whose complex genetics make species boundaries difficult to determine.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Its arching, prickly canes carry five-part leaves with hairy upper surfaces and grey-white, felted undersides. It bears white or pale-pink flowers in woodland clearings and edges.

summary: An evergreen woody shrub native to the Canary Islands. Its rich-green, finely divided leaves are downy, while fragrant blue flowers open from dark-purple buds on branching stems in summer.

Perennial quillwort occurring in the western Mediterranean. It has a short, thick underground stem surrounded by hard, shiny black appendages and many narrow, rigid leaves arranged in a rosette. It grows in temporarily flooded grassland on acidic soils and around pond and stream edges, producing spores in spring.

A bulbous perennial native to the Cape of South Africa, dwarf nerine has narrow leaves and slender pink flowers that appear together in autumn. Its top growth disappears during summer dormancy, and wild plants form large colonies that appear to respond well to frequent fires.
Shrub native from northwestern Argentina through Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay and Peru to Venezuela. It grows in dry scrub and has purple flowers with yellow throats followed by orange berries.
edibilityNote: The species is used as food, but the source does not identify the parts eaten or their preparation.

summary: Evergreen shrub native to eastern Australia, from the Nambucca River to near Gladstone, Queensland. It has broad, elliptical leaves on long stalks. White or lilac flowers appear from late winter to spring, followed by red berries that can remain for many months.

A herb native to South Africa, dune celery grows along the seashore and on sandy hills from Table Bay to Port Natal. It has smooth, upright or sprawling grooved stems, fleshy divided leaves, and flower clusters at the stem tips and sides.
Plant endemic to South Africa’s Northern Cape and Western Cape provinces.
A flowering plant native to Venezuela and Ecuador.

A spore-bearing plant endemic to Macaronesia, Madeira clubmoss occurs in the Azores and Madeira. In the Azores it inhabits humid uplands, lava soils, natural forest undergrowth, ravines and volcanic craters; in Madeira its natural habitat is laurel forest.
Flowering plant native to South Africa, with small, narrow, carrot-like leaves and large green stems. Its flowers are yellow with many long petals, and it is naturalized in New Zealand.

Subtropical succulent flowering plant native to South Africa. It forms dense clusters of ridged branches lined with long spines, which may start red or yellow and darken to black. Damaged plants release toxic white latex.

A small underground-stemmed plant from eastern and southern Africa, it forms a ground-level cluster of slender, succulent leaves. Yellow flowers appear in early summer or after rain, with distinctively tufted stamens.

Large tree native to coastal rainforests of New South Wales and Queensland in eastern Australia. It has exceptionally large leaves, rusty-haired new growth and yellow-orange fruit containing fleshy orange coverings around the seeds. These coverings have an acidic flavour and are eaten raw or made into preserves, sauces, chutneys and cordials.
edibilityNote: The orange fleshy seed coverings are eaten raw and used for jams, jellies, sauces, chutneys and cordials.

summary: Fast-growing shrublet endemic to South Africa’s Cape Province. Its upright, chalky-green, ribbed stems resemble corn cobs and bear scattered blunt, toothpick-like spines near the top. It is poisonous if swallowed, and damaged tissue releases caustic latex that can cause burns and severe reactions.
edibilityNote: The plant is poisonous if ingested; its caustic latex can burn the mouth and may cause throat swelling, anaphylaxis or suffocation.

summary: A rare evergreen Australian shrub found north from the Clarence River in New South Wales, in rainforest margins, riverine scrub and moist eucalyptus-forest gullies. Its long, narrow leaves have stiff, jagged teeth near the base, and its small white-to-mauve flowers are followed by orange-red berries.
A deciduous tree native from India to Japan and south to eastern Australia. It has smooth grey bark, sweetly scented white flowers, and yellow or orange fruit that is sweet and edible to humans.
edibilityNote: The sweet yellow or orange fruit is edible to humans.

summary: An orchid native to Colombia, Trinidad and Venezuela.

A small African ebony-family tree naturally occurring from Cape Town to Tanzania, the bladdernut grows in mountain forests and on rocky slopes. It has strikingly glossy dark-green leaves and fragrant creamy flowers.

An annual flowering plant of unstated native origin, gland clover has a semi-upright habit and leaves divided into three leaflets. It adapts to various soils, from well-drained to periodically waterlogged, and has a very short growing cycle.

A succulent perennial native to South Africa’s semi-arid Karoo, it resembles a small cracked rock through its paired, spotted grey-green or brownish leaves. A new leaf pair replaces an older one yearly, while its yellow-orange flowers open in the afternoon and close at sunset.

A large red alga distributed around the British Isles and from Portugal to Arctic Russia. Its dark-red, flattened, leathery blade is usually unbranched but may split, and it attaches to lower-shore rocks by a disc-like base.

Annual flowering plant recorded from mainland Portugal, although whether it is native there remains unclear. Only two geographically separate mainland subpopulations are known, growing in annual grassland clearings among scrub on basic soils; it is assessed as Vulnerable because only three locations were identified and could disappear quickly under the stated threats.

summary: Red alga found in the coastal waters of Japan.
A woody evergreen perennial vine native to southern Brazil and Argentina. It has tendrilled green leaves and lavender-to-lilac tubular flowers with a pale throat and conspicuous violet veins.

A flowering plant native to Paraguay, northern Argentina, surrounding areas and parts of northeastern Brazil, pink globe amaranth has straight, hairy stems with woody bases. Dense, round purplish-pink flower clusters conceal small, inconspicuous yellow flowers.

An erect shrub or tree endemic to eastern Australia, this geebung grows in near-coastal heath and forest from southeastern Queensland to northeastern New South Wales. It has hairy young branches, broad leaves and groups of yellow flowers, followed by fleshy fruit.

A tetraploid plant of unspecified native origin and a close relative of the domesticated peanut. It is thought to be the peanut's immediate wild ancestor, although it may instead be a weedy descendant of cultivated peanuts.

Tall, branching tree native to the Sikkim Himalaya, Bhutan, Nepal, Malaysia, Indonesia and West Africa, with additional natural populations reported in China, Myanmar, Java and Sumatra. It stands on stilt-like roots and bears very long, finely toothed leaves. Its orange-red, cone-like ripe fruits are sweet and edible.
edibilityNote: The sweet ripe fruit is edible; fruit and seeds are eaten as food or medicine across much of its range.

summary: An orchid, Cymbidium floribundum emits 3-hydroxyoctanoic acid, a signalling chemical recognized by Japanese honeybees.

A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, and originating in the Mediterranean region and southwest Asia. It grows in dry, sunny grassland, scrub clearings and exposed banks, on both limestone and siliceous ground.

sources.title: Hyparrhenia sinaica (Delile) G. Lopez

summary: A rhizomatous perennial native to the Middle East, the Mesopotamian iris has broad grey-green or green leaves. Its branching stems bear scented violet, purple or blue flowers with yellow, orange and white beards.
edibilityNote: The rhizomes and leaves are poisonous if eaten and may cause stomach pain and vomiting.

summary: A plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula, Teucrium gnaphalodes grows at moderate to high elevations and flowers from March to July.

A perennial shrub or subshrub native to temperate South America, including southern Chile, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and northeastern Argentina. It forms clumps with abundant flowers from late summer into early autumn; the flowers are used in infusions and alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks for their bitterness.
edibilityNote: Flowers are used in infusions and alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks for their bitter properties.

summary: A small evergreen succulent native to South Africa. It bears violet flowers and occurs there at elevations of 1,200–1,800 metres.

A vigorous perennial shrub native to the western Mediterranean. It is valued as a pollinator-attracting garden plant and typically grows along evergreen woodland and scrub edges, hedges and roadsides in Portugal, often in shade.
Plant species endemic to Brazil.
A bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It usually grows on basic soils at scrub edges and occurs less often on rocks and fixed coastal dunes.

An annual or biennial flowering plant native to the Indian Subcontinent, China, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, most of Malesia, and Japan. It typically grows in disturbed places and has been introduced widely elsewhere.

Perennial succulent native to southern Africa. Its narrow, pointed, propeller-like leaves are stacked and turn from light green to deep red in sunlight, while small white star-shaped flowers cluster around upright stems in summer.

Biennial herb distributed around the Mediterranean Basin, including Morocco, Madeira, and the Canary Islands. Its white-marked leaves have woolly undersides and strongly thorned edges, while its flower heads range from white or pink to lilac-purple.
edibilityNote: Documented simply as an edible plant; no parts or preparation are specified.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows at the edges or beneath deciduous woodland and scrub, favouring shady, acidic soils rich in organic matter.

sources.title: Euphorbia angulata Jacq.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A rhizomatous perennial whose two listed subspecies are native to mainland Portugal. It has narrow, usually undivided leaves and yellow or pale-yellow flowers. Subspecies aquatilis inhabits freshwater wetlands and rice fields, while subspecies maritimus grows in estuaries, salt marshes and coastal lagoons on wet, salty soils.

sources.title: Sonchus maritimus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant native to the Transcaucasus and Anatolia.

A flowering shrub endemic to south-eastern continental Australia, though naturalised elsewhere in the country. Its narrow leaves have rolled-under edges, and loose clusters of pink-to-red flowers appear mainly from August to December.

A tree native to South America and found in high Andean forests of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. It has a characteristically crooked trunk, cardboard-like leaves, pleasantly scented white flowers and wine-red ripe fruit.
A deciduous tree whose native origin is uncertain, with reports naming Japan, Korea and China. It bears elliptic, sharply toothed leaves and clustered flowers, and its fruit is edible.
edibilityNote: The fruit is edible.

summary: A borage-family plant from the central and southern Iberian Peninsula, Onosma tricerosperma grows in dry, sandy or rocky places. It has branched flowering stems and warted nutlets, usually with three short horns, although these horns are absent in the granatensis subspecies. It flowers in spring.

A flowering plant endemic to the southern Iberian Peninsula, Thymus albicans occurs in Portugal in a restricted part of the Algarve coast. It grows in dry scrub on firm sandy soils and has a fragmented population assessed as Vulnerable in mainland Portugal.

summary: A perennial succulent native to Southern Africa, it grows on partly shaded rocky slopes in bushland. Its fleshy leaves can turn deep ruby-red in full sun, and it bears upright yellow flowers in winter.

A dwarf evergreen flowering shrub native to southern Brazil, Paraguay and northeastern Argentina, Justicia floribunda has downy stems and leaves. Its nodding tubular flowers shade from yellow to scarlet, and one leaf in each pair is smaller than the other.

A flowering herb native to mainland Portugal. It has pale pink flowers and unequal calyx teeth fringed along their length with long hairs, and it grows mainly in sandy meadows, pastures and open woodland.

sources.title: Trifolium sylvaticum Gérard
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A plant species of unstated native origin, it is found in Ecuador and Colombia. Known and newly identified withanolides have been isolated from it.

A shrub or small tree native to eastern Australia, occurring in mountainous rainforest margins, gullies and heathland. Its leaves vary greatly, even on one plant, and cream-to-white flower clusters appear during the native summer; it can resprout from its woody base after bushfire.

A spreading shrub native across the northern Mediterranean from southwestern Spain to western Turkey and Cyprus, it grows mainly on coastal dunes; one isolated tree occurs in southern Portugal. Its broad leaves have a divided white band, while its berry-like cones ripen from green to orange-red, sometimes with a pink waxy coating.

A flowering plant native to Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia. Its leaves yield a fibre called fique, used to make ropes and various woven goods; the flower stalk is also used for structures such as ladders, posts and huts.

sources.title: Furcraea andina Trel., 1915
sources.attribution: Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía de Ecuador - MAE (2025). Listado de plantas de uso y aprovechamiento sostenible en Ecuador. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.60545/eifqjo accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A creeping herb native to South America, white verbena grows in grasslands and beside roads on rich soils. Its pure-white flowers turn violet as they fade, while its small dry fruits split into four one-seeded parts.

A deciduous shrub or small tree native to Japan, including central and southern Honshū, Shikoku and Kyūshū. Its rounded, many-lobed leaves turn gold, orange or dark red in autumn, while its paired winged fruits stand above the foliage and mature from bright red to brown.

A densely branched flowering shrub found in south-central and southeastern China, Taiwan, Vietnam and the Ryukyu Islands. It has reddish stems, small glossy leaves that become reddish-brown, and white funnel-shaped flowers whose pink sepals remain long after flowering.

A herbaceous perennial native to southeast Asia, dense-flowered loosestrife has creeping to rising stems that root at the nodes. Clusters of two to four yellow flowers with red centres appear from spring to summer.

Low spreading or upright shrub endemic to the coastal ranges of south-eastern New South Wales. It has oblong to egg-shaped leaves and clusters of red or pink flowers tipped with cream or yellow, flowering mainly in winter and spring.
Spreading succulent native to the southwestern Cape Provinces of South Africa. It typically grows in sandy areas.
A flowering plant native to Ukraine, Crimea, southern European Russia and the Caucasus. It resists hollyhock rust and is hardy to USDA zone 4.
A lily native to the mountains of central China, including Guizhou, Hubei and Jiangxi. Its unscented orange flowers have black spots and petals that bend backward as they mature.
Perennial herb native to southern Europe and parts of northern temperate Asia. It has large, fleshy leaves and inconspicuous white flowers and seeds borne in long clusters atop a stalk.

A lily native to mainland China, Hong Kong, Kinmen, the Matsu Islands, northern and central Vietnam, and Kachin in Myanmar. Its variety Lilium brownii var. viridulum is often cultivated for its edible bulbs.
edibilityNote: The bulbs of Lilium brownii var. viridulum are edible, and this variety is often cultivated for them.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it is restricted to moist meadows on sandy soil near the eastern Algarve coast, where the assessed population had only about 20 mature plants and was classified as Critically Endangered.

summary: Evergreen tree native to southern Japan and eastern and southern China. It has unusually large, glossy, leathery leaves with toothed but non-spiny edges, and dense clusters of fruit that ripen from orange-red to dark red in winter. Its leaves may be infused to make bitter nail tea.
edibilityNote: Leaves may be infused to make tea called “bitter nail tea.”

summary: A perennial flowering plant native from the Caucasus and northern Iran through parts of Central Asia to Mongolia and Afghanistan, Primula algida bears clusters of mauve to violet flowers. It grows in moist alpine grassland and wet meadows, as well as on south-facing rocky ledges, cliffs and slopes.

A milkvetch species native to the western Mediterranean, Astragalus glaux grows in low scrub, usually thyme scrub, on marl soils. In mainland Portugal, assessments conducted in 2016–2019 found it restricted to a few populations in Beira Litoral and Alto Alentejo and classified it as Vulnerable.
