summary: A flowering legume; its subspecies nummularioides is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to Macaronesia, Patellifolia procumbens occurs in Madeira.

A flowering tree native to Africa, the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent. Young trees bear paired straight spines, while mature trees commonly lack them, and the flowers form bright golden-yellow heads. In India it is used in dishes; Maasai people eat the inner bark and fruit pulp boiled in water.
edibilityNote: Used in Indian dishes; Maasai people eat the inner bark and fruit pulp boiled in water.

summary: A flowering plant native to Madeira.

A perennial shrub endemic to Madeira and native to its evergreen forest. It has a woody trunk topped by rosettes of long, glossy, toothed leaves, giving it a giant-dandelion appearance. Yellow, dandelion-like flowers appear in summer.

A perennial subshrub endemic to Madeira Island and Deserta Grande. Its thick leaves vary with growing conditions, and its flower stalk is notably sticky; new small flowering stalks may continue appearing for several months.

A perennial flowering subshrub native to Brazil, the goldfish plant climbs trees in its natural habitat. It has small, fleshy, usually waxy dark-green leaves and brilliant orange summer flowers shaped somewhat like plump goldfish or clogs.

An evergreen shrub or tree native from central southern Africa north through several tropical African uplands. Its dense, much-branched crown and dull bluish foliage are distinctive, and female plants bear berries that turn from green through reddish-brown to black when ripe.

An annual flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits sparse mountain grasslands on rocky or gravelly ground; in Portugal it occurs in the mountains of Trás-os-Montes and Beira Interior.

An annual flowering plant native to southern South America, including Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and southeastern Brazil. Its purple, pink or white flowers have six conspicuously long stamens, while glandular hairs can give the plant a skunky smell.
A plant presumed to originate in South America. It is naturalised in Portugal in wet meadows, beside waterways and in landscaped urban spaces, and is legally classed as invasive in Madeira.
A herbaceous perennial native to central Chile, it spreads from underground stems. Its flowers have deep violet or pink-lilac outer parts and yellow-striped inner parts marked with wine-red lines.
A perennial flowering plant native to KwaZulu-Natal, Lesotho, Mpumalanga, the Eastern Cape and the Western Cape.

A sturdy, shrubby climber endemic to south-western Western Australia. It has narrow, softly hairy leaves and nodding blue, white or pink flowers; its green spindle-shaped berries turn purplish with age.
A large shrub endemic to the southwestern Cape Provinces of South Africa. It turns bright yellow during its winter flowering season.
A slow-growing succulent tree native from South Africa north to Mozambique. Africa’s largest aloe-like plant, it bears rose-pink, green-tipped tubular flowers in winter.
Annual grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in mountain fields, fallow ground and pastures, especially on dry, acidic, sandy soils derived from granite.

An annual daisy endemic to Australia, growing naturally in dry, shallow or rocky soils. It has finely divided leaves and white, mauve or pink flowerheads, which appear mainly from early autumn to midwinter but may occur throughout the year.
A hawkweed species native to Spain.
Low, spreading flowering shrub endemic to south-eastern Australia. Its trailing wiry stems scramble over other vegetation, ending in pale to bright yellow flowers; flowering occurs in most months.
Flowering plant native to Peru, northwestern Argentina and central Chile. An early account recorded it beside rivers near Concepción, Chile.

summary: Low-growing, solitary rosette-forming aloe found mainly from northwestern Eswatini through Mpumalanga to Limpopo, South Africa. Its dark-lined green leaves have prominent reddish-brown toothed edges, while its branched flower stalks bear dull brick-red to coral-red flowers.

sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Plant species native to southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and northern Argentina. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental and has three recognized varieties.

A succulent evergreen shrub native to South Africa's semidesert Little Karoo, bear-paws has chunky, fuzzy green leaves. The typical subspecies has reddish teeth at the leaf tips, while the other recognized subspecies generally lacks them; orange bell-shaped flowers appear in spring.
edibilityNote: The plant is known to be poisonous to humans, livestock and dogs.

summary: A fern endemic to the Azores, Madeira, and Canary Islands, it grows in shaded volcanic-rock crevices and walls within laurel and mountain pine forests. Its leathery fronds have a thick, bright reddish-brown central stalk bearing three wings, including a distinctive lower wing. There have been no records from the Azores since 1972.

Small epiphytic fern endemic to Terceira and Flores in the Azores and reported from Pico, where its continued existence is uncertain. It inhabits the wettest, windiest parts of moss-covered juniper rainforest, and its fronds have prominent black-edged margins. Fewer than 100 individuals are reported in the wild.
A bulb-forming herb native to parts of Mediterranean Europe and North Africa, including several islands, and associated with the Black Sea region. It has yellow flowers.
A bulbous plant native to Mongolia, Siberia, the Russian Far East, Korea and northern China. It has slender, grass-like leaves and scented, nodding red flowers that may be spotted with black.
edibilityNote: In Taiwan, the flowers and bulbs are used as food.

summary: A long-lived bulbous perennial native to western Sichuan in southwestern China, it bears strongly fragrant, trumpet-shaped white flowers with yellow throats and purple-flushed exteriors. The fragrance is especially strong at night.
A corm-forming plant native to South Africa’s dry-summer, wet-winter region. It is dormant in summer and is valued as an ornamental and cut flower.

A flowering shrub native to southwestern South Africa, red sugarbush grows on dry, stony upper mountain slopes. It forms a rounded plant and flowers from September to January. Fire destroys the plant, but its seeds survive and are dispersed by wind.

Succulent perennial native to the southern coast of South Africa. Its pink, purple or white flowers are followed by sweet fruits that are less sour than those of related species. The edible fruits are locally made into traditional preserves.
edibilityNote: The sweet fruits are edible and are locally used to make traditional preserves.

summary: An annual, or sometimes perennial, flowering plant native to low-lying regions and coastal plains of South Africa’s Western Cape. It forms a basal cluster of leaves and has yellow-to-orange flowers, usually marked with black or brown spots. Its slender leaves are smooth above and woolly beneath.
Flowering plant native to Brazil.

Sturdy succulent native to the Karoo mountains of South Africa, extending into Lesotho. Its stems and leaf sheaths have dark-green stripes, while its recurved leaves have many small white teeth; it tolerates frost and some light snow.

A low-growing succulent annual native to South Africa’s Cape Peninsula. Its many-petalled, daisy-like flowers come in numerous bright colours and open in strong sunlight, while reflective, water-storing cells give the leaves a glistening surface.

An upright or sprawling shrub native to South Africa and endemic to the Western Cape, it bears large flower heads containing hundreds of small flowers. Its seed-bearing fruits remain enclosed in old dried flower heads retained on the plant.
Plant endemic to KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern and Western Cape provinces of South Africa.
A small to medium tree of unspecified native origin, with large, finely toothed leaves marked by many straight, prominent veins. It has pink flowers in branched clusters and round berries.

Evergreen shrub or small tree endemic to far southwestern South Africa, it grows slowly and usually remains fairly small. Its young leaves are red, and it bears small, pale-red berries that are edible and were formerly eaten by the Indigenous people described in the source as “Hottentots.”
edibilityNote: The berries are edible and were formerly eaten by the Indigenous people described in the source as “Hottentots.”

summary: Flowering plant native only to the Cape Provinces of South Africa. It has a stemless growth habit.
Flowering plant native to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini. It has been introduced to Ireland and Tasmania.

A deciduous tree native to Japan, the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan and southern China. Its variety fauriei has been crossed with Lagerstroemia indica to produce widely planted ornamental hybrid crepe myrtles.

Perennial nettle found in Japan, China and Taiwan, where it inhabits moist mountain forests. Its stinging hairs can cause pain, redness, burning or itching. After boiling to destroy its toxicity, it is used in Taiwan in soup, bread, shortbread and fried leaves.
edibilityNote: Boiling destroys its toxicity; Taiwanese uses include soup, bread, Chinese shortbread and crispy fried leaves.

summary: Mat-forming herb native to Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Paraguay and Uruguay, growing as an annual or short-lived perennial. Its dense flower spikes have papery, shiny segments coloured whitish to pink; eating the plant causes nervous-system problems in horses.

A variably hairy biennial or perennial daisy occurring in South Africa’s Western and Eastern Cape provinces. Its branches can root where their joints touch soil, and individual flower heads have blue rays surrounding yellow centres. Recognised subspecies differ in leaf shape, flower-head size and glandular hairs.
An evergreen flowering shrub endemic to South Africa’s Western and Eastern Cape provinces, this conebush is characteristic of montane fynbos vegetation.
A flowering plant endemic to Brazil.

A shrub native to southern Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Its yellow to orange-red bell-shaped flowers have strong dark-red veins. The flowers are edible raw or cooked, becoming sweeter the longer they remain open.
edibilityNote: The flowers are edible raw or cooked, with sweetness increasing as each bloom remains open.

summary: A flowering succulent native to Namibia, Botswana, northern South Africa, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, Huernia zebrina has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

Succulent plant reported as native to South Africa, though its origin is uncertain and it may be a hybrid. Its densely arranged, blue, sickle-shaped leaves are narrow, elongated and rounded in cross-section.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Carex helodes is endemic to the western Mediterranean. It grows in wet meadows, temporarily waterlogged soils and beside temporary waterways. Most of its global distribution is concentrated in mainland Portugal, but few recent records exist and its current national population is poorly understood.

summary: A perennial plant with no stated native origin, it is found in South Africa’s Cape Provinces and Free State. Its paired green-grey leaves resemble round stones and split along a fissure through which tiny white flowers emerge. Each flowering pair is replaced annually by a new pair as the old leaves shrivel.
An evergreen perennial herb from South Africa, red pypie bears bright red flowers in spring. It grows in sandy soils near the coast at low elevations.
A woody shrublet native to South Africa. It has small pink flowers and waxy, slightly fringed green leaves with a sweet, mildly spicy scent; the aromatic leaves are used in potpourri.

Succulent native to South Africa’s Cape Provinces, Free State and Northern Provinces. In the wild, usually only its leaf tips rise above the sand or dust, patterned with irregular white, grey or pink dots resembling local pebbles.
A rhizomatous plant native to the southwestern and southern Cape Provinces, where it grows mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

summary: A flowering plant endemic to South Africa’s Cape Provinces. It is common in sandy coastal habitats, and was used at the Cape to promote sweating and urination.

A perennial herb native from Eritrea to southern Africa, Madagascar and nearby Indian Ocean islands, and the Arabian Peninsula. Its slender stems twine or trail, bearing heart-shaped to arrow-shaped leaves and small pinkish, pale purple or white flowers.

summary: A small succulent endemic to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province. Its green triangular leaves curve inward and bear narrow white ridges only on their outer surfaces, while the inner surfaces are smooth. It is rare in cultivation and is often confused with Haworthiopsis attenuata.

A small evergreen succulent from South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province. Its tapered leaves form rosettes and bear bands of white bumps on both surfaces, distinguishing it from the similar Haworthiopsis fasciata; it also readily produces offsets and forms large wild clumps.
An evergreen, spiny succulent shrub endemic to South Africa’s southern Cape Province. It has thick, segmented blue-green branches and spreads underground to form extensive dense stands.

A succulent perennial native to coastal KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, it also occurs naturally into the Eastern Cape and Mozambique. It has bright pink to mauve flowers, dull green triangular leaves and a distinctively double-ridged, barrel-shaped flower base.
edibilityNote: The fruits are edible.

summary: A bulb-forming plant found in the summer-rain bushveld of South Africa's Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal provinces. It grows singly or in small groups, with above-ground pear-shaped bulbs and a rosette of glossy, dark-green leaves. Upright white flowers with green mid-stripes appear from midsummer into autumn.

A rare, endangered aloe from Southern Africa, it usually forms a single, stemless rosette with upright, waxy sea-green leaves. Young leaves are thorny on both surfaces, but most thorns disappear as the plant ages; its two varieties have restricted ranges, and the species may also occur in Eswatini.

A tree-like aloe indigenous to summer-rainfall areas of southern Africa, naturally occurring in southeastern South Africa, Eswatini and southern Mozambique. Its upright flower clusters open from tightly packed yellow buds, with bright red stamens producing a fluffy bottlebrush look. It is usually single-stemmed in nature, with a thin trunk and a dense rosette of grooved, dull-green leaves.

Rapidly growing climbing succulent native to dry vegetation of South Africa's Eastern Cape, extending into the Western Cape border. Its recurved fleshy leaves act as hooks, while soft white hair-like teeth run around the stem at each leaf base.

Bushy, many-branched succulent native to grasslands and thickets of Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, South Africa. Its thin, greyish-green leaves do not curve backward and have tiny white marginal teeth. It flowers throughout the year, especially in winter, usually with bright yellow blooms.
A small succulent endemic to quartz gravel in South Africa’s Knersvlakte region, Western Cape. Its thick leaves resemble an egg cut in half, and its flowers are purple with yellow centres.

A perennial vine native to the Cape Provinces, Madagascar and Namibia, weeping asparagus is known as bridal veil. It has been introduced to Central America and parts of Australia and is considered invasive in some areas.
An aquatic flowering herb of lowland wetlands. It may grow above the water or drift submerged; the supplied sources disagree about its native origin.

sources.title: Callitriche deflexa A.Braun
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A dioecious shrub native to southern Africa, it has green, wart-marked twigs and bluish-green leaves sometimes mixed with bright orange ones. Its spherical, three-chambered capsules may also bear warts and burst open when dry to release their seeds.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal, Corynephorus fasciculatus is not protected under Portuguese or European Union law.

A low-growing succulent native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape, originating in the southern Drakensberg region. Its spreading stems carry finger-like blue-grey leaves that develop maroon tips in dry conditions, alongside yellow daisy-like flowers on slender stems.

A succulent groundcover and dwarf shrub native to South Africa's Cape Province. It forms dense, low mats of silvery-blue, finger-like fleshy leaves and bears small pompom-like flowers, usually from spring to autumn.
An annual grass, it grows in wet or waterlogged meadows in Portugal.
A plant endemic to KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa.

Rapidly growing woody vine native to tropical dry forests from Mexico through Brazil and northern Argentina, and the Caribbean. It climbs using small aerial roots, produces yellow trumpet flowers and large underground tubers, and can spread through every forest layer.

A low shrublet found in South Africa’s Western and Eastern Cape provinces. Its rigid, leathery leaves are mostly alternate, while blue outer florets surround yellow central florets; it flowers year-round.
A shrub described as South African, though its native status is not explicitly stated. It favors damp ground, riverbanks and marshy areas from the Western Cape through the Eastern Cape.

Agave-family plant reportedly native to Colombia and Ecuador, though its range is uncertain and cultivated source material apparently came from Quetzaltenango, Guatemala. It has rough, dark-green, sword-shaped leaves with hooked brown teeth. Its tall, loosely branched flower stalk bears many bulbils.

A succulent native to the Western Cape of South Africa. Its rough, sometimes wavy leaves grow in two opposite rows, while its small pink flowers have swollen bases and appear from September to December.

An evergreen perennial herb of unstated native origin, it occurs on sandstone and granite slopes in southwestern Cape Province, South Africa. Its drooping flowers are red and tubular with yellow throats, their centers difficult to see without bending down.

A small, clump-forming plant endemic to South Africa’s Eastern Cape, it has rosettes of thick, light-green leaves. Its soft, boat-shaped leaves usually have transparent streaks near their tips, which may be the only parts visible above the sand in the wild.

A flowering succulent from South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, now also naturalized in Mexico. It forms large clumps of long stems crowded with thick leaves, usually dark green but sometimes turning rich purple-red in full sunlight.
A flowering plant native to southeastern Africa, specifically southern Mozambique, Swaziland, KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga. It is relatively widespread and has several varieties.

A flowering succulent from South Africa’s Western and Eastern Cape provinces, Haworthiopsis viscosa packs pointed, rough leaves into three tiers along its stems. It produces offsets at the base and can eventually form large clumps. Several regional varieties are recognized, including a variable-leaved form from near Joubertina.

A scrambling climber or shrub native to Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Eswatini and South Africa. It produces masses of scented, white, star-shaped flowers from late spring through summer and attracts various birds.

A succulent shrub or small tree endemic to a few mountains in South Africa’s Western Cape. Its tongue-shaped leaves form striking fans on paired branches, and from August to October it produces masses of bright pink flowers.
A succulent endemic to South Africa's Western Cape, it forms part of the fynbos vegetation.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A succulent endemic to the Western Cape, the Sandveld brightfig grows in fynbos from Redelinghuys to the Cape Peninsula and Agulhas Plain. About half its habitat has been lost to development, farming and invasive plants.
A succulent endemic to South Africa's Western Cape, it forms part of the fynbos vegetation. Its range extends from Tulbagh to Worcester and the Langeberg.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A succulent endemic to South Africa’s Western Cape, with a population described as stable.

A critically endangered succulent endemic to the Cape Flats Dune Strandveld around Cape Town, South Africa. It is tiny with bright pink and violet flowers, and only two fragmented patches totalling roughly 100 plants remain.

A rock-dwelling plant found in South Africa’s summer-rainfall areas, though not endemic there. Each leaf-pair flowers and is replaced by a new pair as the old one shrivels; collection for medicinal markets has contributed to declining numbers.
Succulent plant native to South Africa. Its usually grey leaves have irregular channels across their tops, often with red, blue-pink, brown or green tinges, and it bears yellow flowers.
A shrub native to the far west of South Africa’s Western Cape. It has formidable straight woody thorns, leathery clustered leaves and tubular purple flowers; its ripe berries are very dark red.
edibilityNote: The fruit’s safety for people is unclear; the edibility of other Lycium species does not establish its safety.

summary: A tall shrub endemic to southwestern Western Australia. It has pale, waxy-looking leaves and bright-red flower spikes in spring, and grows on swampy sandy or clay soils.
An open, straggly shrub endemic to South Australia and Victoria. It has stiff, sharply pointed leaves and summer spikes of bright red bottlebrush flowers tipped with yellow.

A creeping succulent perennial native to South Africa's Eastern Cape Province, heart-leaf ice plant forms low mats from a woody base. It has fleshy, heart-shaped textured leaves and solitary magenta-purple flowers that open by day but close at night and on cloudy days.
Erect shrub endemic to New Caledonia and the Loyalty Islands. Its unusually thin, papery leaves and smooth white flowers distinguish it from the other Myoporum species found in New Caledonia.

A perennial herb native to southern Louisiana and Texas, clockweed has pink or white four-petalled flowers with long, hairlike stamens. It flowers from early spring until the first frost, and some cultivars open white at dawn before turning pink and falling by dusk.

Resprouting shrub endemic to South Africa's Cape Provinces, especially dry, stony ground from Namaqualand and the Karoo to the Eastern Cape. It has narrow, hairy, often silvery leaves and mainly violet-blue flowers, and can resprout after fire.

A small, spreading pelargonium native to South Africa. Its waxy green leaves have a distinct apple scent, and it bears pale pink flowers. In Cyprus, the leaves flavour cake and pastry syrups and are sometimes preserved and eaten as a spoon sweet.
edibilityNote: In Cyprus, leaves flavour cake and pastry syrups or are preserved and eaten as a spoon sweet.

summary: A poplar tree native to northeastern China and Mongolia, it is commonly planted along streets in cool temperate parts of Europe. It has also been introduced to North America, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand.

A deciduous oak native to the Caucasus and Iran’s Alborz Mountains. It has narrow leaves with many regular triangular lobes and two-toned acorns held in cups densely covered with soft, mossy bristles.

Herbaceous perennial native to northeastern Asia, including northern Japan and far eastern Russia. Strong spreading underground stems form large colonies bearing unusually large, nearly heart-shaped leaves. Its tender shoots are edible.
edibilityNote: Tender shoots are edible.

summary: An evergreen succulent shrub native to Southern Africa. Its fleshy trunk bears densely packed, finger-like leaves, while fragrant golden-yellow flower clusters appear in winter and attract butterflies.

A deciduous tree of African savannas from West Africa to South Africa. It resists drought, has hard termite-resistant wood, and provides flowers, foliage and seed pods browsed by giraffes and other mammals.

A flowering shrub native to the Western Cape of South Africa, restricted to the Hottentots Holland Mountains from the Slanghoek Mountains to Franschhoek. Fire kills the plant but its seeds survive, and ants carry fallen fruits into their nests.

Biennial to short-lived perennial herb native to South Africa's Eastern Cape. Its fragrant flowers open at night, and the root can be harvested after the second year. Xhosa traditional healers use the root during initiation to induce vivid, reportedly prophetic lucid dreams.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, but introduced in the Azores.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

An evergreen tree of unstated native origin, Natal mahogany is found from South Africa’s KwaZulu-Natal Province to tropical Africa. It has glossy dark green leaves, a wide crown and sweet-scented flowers; its black seeds are almost enclosed by bright red coverings, and its fruit is emetic.
edibilityNote: The fruit is described as emetic, but the source does not explicitly call it inedible or poisonous.

summary: An annual herb found across most of southern and central Europe, Turkey and the Caucasus. Its hairy, branching stems bear rounded purple or pink flower heads, and the plant self-pollinates.

sources.title: Trifolium diffusum Ehrh.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in cultivated fields, along roads and beside waterways, especially in disturbed places.
Plant endemic to KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape.

A medium-sized shrub endemic to New South Wales and Queensland, Australia, with narrow, rigid-pointed leaves. Its red flower spikes appear in late spring or early summer and are followed by woody capsules.

Herbaceous perennial native to the western Mediterranean. It has purple flowers from spring through autumn and commonly grows from limestone rock faces, walls or roadsides. Its populations often occupy small ranges.

A small evergreen shrub native to Madeira, it is rare and grows mainly in damp laurel-forest edges and clearings in the island’s northeast. Its branching growth bears densely hairy leaves and small white to violet-purple flowers.
A perennial spiny shrub endemic to the northwestern Iberian Peninsula, it grows in humid scrub, peatlands and beside waterways. Its flower clusters contain three to five flowers.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An elderberry species endemic to Madeira Island in the eastern Atlantic Ocean.
An aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, thin-leaved horned-pondweed inhabits ponds and marshes. It grows in fresh or moderately brackish water.
A flowering plant endemic to Cape Verde, now found only on Santo Antão, São Nicolau and Santiago. It is considered extinct on São Vicente, Boa Vista and Maio.

A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal, Adenocarpus anisochilus occurs mainly in the south and southwest, with an isolated population near Sintra. It grows in scrub beside forests, cork-oak woods and waterways, favouring deep acidic soils, and readily colonises abandoned forestry and farmland.

An arum-family plant native to Asia and Africa, where it grows in forests and riverside meadows. Its yellowish, purple-spotted floral sheath and purple spike appear before the green leaf. Mature flowers smell powerfully of rotting meat, and the plant generates its own heat.
A plant native to southern Madeira and the Canary Islands of Lanzarote and Fuerteventura. It has dark green leaves with fine, widely spaced whitish hairs and puffed yellow, pea-like flowers.

Fern native to Madeira, the Canary and Cape Verde islands, and patchy parts of East Africa, Madagascar, the Mascarene Islands, Comoros and Chad’s Tibesti. It grows in sheltered rock crevices and on walls, with large round leaves marked by branching veins and a very narrow red edge.

A flowering shrub endemic to south-eastern Australia, it grows in woodland and forest from near Mount Kosciuszko to eastern Victoria. Young branches and leaves bear brownish hairs, while clustered yellow flowers are followed by oval fruit that turns from green to purplish.

A shrub endemic to Macaronesia, Canary Hare's Ear occurs on Madeira, Porto Santo, El Hierro and La Gomera, with different varieties and subspecies having narrower ranges. It has narrow grey-green leaves and loose, elongated clusters of yellow flowers.

A herbaceous plant originating in the Canary Islands, Andryala glandulosa has leaves with wavy, curled edges and flower heads carried on long stalks. Its subspecies have differing distributions across the Canary Islands and Madeira.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.

A perennial herb whose native origin is not explicitly supplied, rough-leaved phlomis has a narrow Mediterranean distribution extending into Transcaucasia, Anatolia and the Maghreb. Its rough, opposite leaves accompany tiers of purple, two-lipped flowers, and it inhabits dry pastures, disturbed ground and slopes.

summary: A densely woolly shrub endemic to Madeira, Porto Santo and Bugio. Its foliage is white to greyish, and it bears creamy-yellow flowers from March to July in sunny clearings and open places.

An upright evergreen shrub native to Madeira and the central and western Canary Islands, this plant has slender branches and narrow to broad lance-shaped leaves. Its pale powder-blue or whitish flower heads are dense, rounded and usually crowded near the stem tips.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.

An evergreen perennial foxglove native to Portugal and Spain, with rose-red flowers in summer. Its two subspecies differ notably in flower colour and the hairs on their flowering stems, and both grow in rocky cracks.

A flowering plant originating in the Canary Islands. It forms a robust, dense shrub with long divided leaves and clusters of white-rayed flower heads; its two subspecies occur respectively on Tenerife and La Gomera.
Flowering plant native to Portugal's Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira Archipelago.

A primarily epiphytic flowering bromeliad endemic to southeastern Brazil, Aechmea pectinata occurs from Rio de Janeiro State south to Paraná and Santa Catarina. It is found mainly along the coast, including several protected areas.

A tree native to India, southern China, Indo-China and Malesia, Ficus callosa may develop large supporting roots at its base. Young trees have larger, lobed leaves, while mature green-yellow figs grow singly or in pairs at the leaf joints.

A perennial marine red alga recorded from the northeastern Atlantic, Mediterranean and Black Sea. Its firm, bright-red fronds have flattened sides, fork repeatedly and can form dense mats that provide habitat for other organisms.
A flowering plant native to Madeira and the Canary Islands.

An annual herb occurring in Southern Europe, North Africa, the Canary Islands and the Middle East, spiny starwort bears solitary yellow flower heads with long, hairy bracts ending in sharp spines. It flowers from May through July.
A perennial herb of unstated native origin, reported from France, Spain and Portugal. It has a tuberous underground stem, yellow flower heads and hairy fruits topped with bristles or scales.

sources.title: Jasonia tuberosa (Linnaeus 1753)
sources.attribution: Jarvis C, admin (2007). Chapter 7: Linnaean Plant Names and their Types (part E). Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.291971 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A perennial herb endemic to Australia, common sneezeweed grows especially in damp, flood-prone ground. Its distinctively shaped leaves have a pungent pine-like, minty scent, while its flower heads are tiny and usually green.
A plant native to Europe, western Siberia, the western Himalayas, the Canary Islands and Morocco, field fluffweed belongs to the daisy family.

A small deciduous tree described as endemic to Spain’s Cantabrian range, with additional occurrences in the Iberian System near Teruel. Often stunted or shrubby, it has late-emerging leaves with uneven rounded lobes. Its small, nearly round acorns have flattened bases and slightly squared-off tips.

A deciduous shrub native to the central and eastern United States and Ontario. Its golden-yellow flowers have five petals and numerous stamens, and it grows in places including riversides, thickets, swamp edges and oak woodlands.

Small deciduous tree native to North America, from eastern Texas and southern Oklahoma to Durango in Mexico. It grows naturally on dry, rocky slopes, often over limestone, and bears purple early-spring flowers on separate male and female trees.
A short, densely branched shrub native to Western Sahara, Morocco and the Canary Islands, it has pale yellow flowers. Dense short hairs give its oval leaves a greyish appearance.
A multicellular red marine alga recorded in Europe and Africa; its native origin is not specified.

A flowering subshrub with no native origin specified, Madeira sorrel grows on Madeira and the western Canary Islands. Its triangular-oval leaves wither at the base, and it favours rocky, humid, shady slopes and ravines.
A perennial herb native and endemic to Gran Canaria. It has a thick rhizome, rounded leaves and flower heads with white-to-carmine petals around purple centres.
An annual herb native to parts of China, growing in forests and grassy places on hillsides and plains. It has upright or trailing stems and blue-purple or purple flowers arranged in groups of six.
A tree or shrub native to the Canary Islands, where it occurs on Gran Canaria, Tenerife and La Gomera. It grows in warm woodland and has rough bark and compound leaves with ten pairs of leaflets.
A perennial herb endemic to the Canary Islands off northwest Africa. It has long, grass-like leaves.

A herb native to Macaronesia and endemic to the Canary Islands. It has simple leaves and tiny white or pinkish, two-lipped flowers arranged in roughly spherical clusters. Its two varieties occupy partly overlapping groups of islands.
A bromeliad endemic to Brazil. It grows either on other plants or on rocks.

A wild potato native to South America, including Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, Peru, Uruguay, and Paraguay. It commonly grows as a weed in disturbed ground and contains compounds associated with resistance to Colorado potato beetles.
An annual herb recorded from Santa Maria, Madeira, the Desertas and Porto Santo. It is densely hairy, with broad leaves often tinged purple-red, and bears a few deep-yellow flowers.
Annual flowering plant native to the Mediterranean region. In summer, it produces shallow, funnel-shaped flowers in white and pink, with maroon centres and veining.

Leafy moss with no native origin explicitly stated, distributed across the Northern Hemisphere. It forms low, loose, glossy yellow-green to dark-green mats, mainly on deciduous-tree bark, and produces spore capsules very frequently, sometimes with two generations present together.

A semi-evergreen twining vine, it has five bright-green leaflets and fragrant purple-red spring flowers in long hanging clusters. Purple, sausage-shaped fruits may follow if cross-pollination occurs between separate species or varieties.
edibilityNote: The species is described as edible and produces purple fruits, although their flavour is undocumented.

summary: A red alga found in shallow coastal waters across several East Asian countries. Its branching body ranges from purple and red to yellowish-red; it is eaten in salads and other dishes and used to make agar, including for desserts.
edibilityNote: Used historically for Japanese tokoroten and now for agar, salads, puddings, jams and other dishes in producing regions.

summary: An epiphytic bromeliad native to Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Paraguay. Its long, branching stems tend to hang, while overlapping leaves are thickly covered with tiny white hairs; its short-lived white flowers usually self-pollinate.
A red alga recorded along the coasts of South Africa and Namibia.

Rhizomatous evergreen herbaceous perennial native to Japan, China and Korea. It bears dense spikes of pale yellow flowers followed by tight clusters of red berries. The plant is generally regarded as inedible and possibly toxic.
edibilityNote: The plant is generally regarded as inedible and possibly toxic; no particular part or preparation is specified.

summary: A shrub native to the Ibero-Mauritanian region around the Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa. It has three-part leaves, yellow flowers that may occur in groups of three, and hairy seed pods.

Evergreen perennial or small shrub native to Sicily and southern Italy. It has narrow leaves with a strong white midrib and green-and-yellow summer flowers; all parts are toxic if swallowed, and cut stems release irritating milky sap.
edibilityNote: All parts are toxic if ingested.

summary: An annual herb native to the Greater Antilles and the southeastern United States from Florida to Louisiana, it has many small flower heads arranged in elongated arrays and tight clumps. Each head bears a few purple central flowers but no ray flowers.
A low-growing perennial native to the Mediterranean region, it has trailing stems and wild flowers that may be blue or orange. White forms also exist, while a red form was developed through breeding.

A climbing flowering plant native to Taiwan and Japan’s Ryukyu Islands, it produces smooth, round leaves and tiny white flowers. It is not particularly rare in Taiwan but is listed as critically endangered in Japan.

A mat-forming perennial with dark-green, hairy evergreen leaves and masses of five-lobed blue or white flowers. White-flowered plants exist, but garden varieties are especially valued for abundant, intensely azure blooms.

An evergreen flowering shrub native to central and southern China, Taiwan, and Luzon in the Philippines, Chinese evergreen viburnum forms a dense, rounded bush. It is used in landscaping and is hardy to USDA zone 7.

Rosette-forming succulent native to Venezuela and also found in parts of Colombia and the Leeward Islands. It has fleshy, spined leaves and a tall central stalk bearing hundreds of yellow flowers. Cooked leaves and the baked central portion are eaten, while cooked plant material also yields sugary juice that is fermented and distilled into cocuy liquor.
edibilityNote: Cooked leaves and the baked centre are eaten; cooked plant material also provides sugary juice for fermented and distilled cocuy liquor.

summary: Flowering plant native to southern Europe, occurring from Portugal, Spain, France and Italy eastward through parts of the Balkans to Crimea.

A small cactus native to Nuevo León and Coahuila, Mexico, where it grows in desert and dry scrub. Its rounded, densely spined stems produce tiny pink daytime flowers followed in summer by slender, bright-red fruits that quickly become papery.
A flowering plant in the mint family, Sideritis arborescens is recorded in Portugal, but the supplied information does not establish that it is native there.

A mat-forming evergreen stonecrop native to northwestern and southwestern Europe and northern Africa. Its creeping shoots root as they spread, while upright stems bear bright-yellow flowers; it is edible and can be added to salads and soups.
edibilityNote: The plant is edible and may be added to salads and soups.

summary: A medium-sized deciduous tree native to South, East and Southeast Asia. It has grey bark, opposite leaves divided into toothed leaflets, large clusters of white flowers and nuts with long, narrow wings.

A succulent endemic to Madeira Island and the Desertas Islands, typically growing on rocky cliffs, walls, ravines and similar sites. It is usually smooth and green, with an ascending dark-green stem and dense clusters of pale golden-yellow flowers, most with seven petals.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Features still requiring confirmation include basal leaf rosettes with long, slender runners and leaves that are nearly hairless above but densely covered with short, branched hairs beneath.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in rock crevices and on limestone outcrops.

A medium-sized red marine alga, it is recorded from Norway to Morocco, the Mediterranean, Canary Islands, Channel Islands and British Isles. It grows upright with whorled, hollow branches that have regular constrictions and a gelatinous texture. Its colour is pinkish or purple.
An annual flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on acidic soils in fallow fields, disturbed scrub and roadsides.
Herb native to South Africa's Cape Provinces. Its best-known subspecies, the Antique White Freesia, has become naturalized in California, the Mediterranean Basin and parts of the Southern Hemisphere.

A member of the borage family whose native origin is not stated. Its dried root is used in Chinese herbal medicine and was cultivated in Japan for medicine and costly, light-sensitive purple textile dye.

Evergreen flowering tree or large shrub endemic to central and southern continental Chile, Sophora macrocarpa has long, slender branches and reddish-brown hairs on new growth. Its hanging flower clusters bear long yellow petals, and it flowers from August to December.

A variable shrub or tree native to the high Andes from Peru’s Cordillera Blanca to Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, and also to Ecuador. Its small leathery leaves are dark green above and cinnamon-brown beneath, while its scented yellow-orange flowers deepen to orange-red with age.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on acidic soils along scrub and woodland edges, paths and meadows, often near waterways where the surface is temporarily moist.

sources.title: Dorycnopsis gerardi (L.) Boiss.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A bulb-forming perennial native to Iran and Kyrgyzstan, Persian onion bears spherical clusters of many purple to reddish-purple, star-shaped flowers in late spring and early summer. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental.

A flowering herb native to Portugal and, within mainland Portugal, confined to the Algarve. It grows in rocky grasslands, scrub clearings and stony limestone areas, and was assessed there as Vulnerable because of continuing habitat and population decline.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits sparse meadows in scrub clearings and beneath evergreen woods or pines; reported but unconfirmed traits include a slender stem and flattened flower clusters with fewer than ten upward-pointing rays.

A perennial flowering plant native throughout the Mediterranean Basin, pale stonecrop has overlapping, pointed, fleshy dark-green leaves that are often bluish-grey. In midsummer, it produces upright stems topped with clusters of small greenish-white to creamy flowers, followed by dark-brown fruit.
edibilityNote: Its leaves may be used in cooking as a pot-herb.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in sparse meadows, pastures and open scrub clearings on rocky limestone or dolomite ground.

A large, leafless orchid found from the central Himalayas to Thailand. It lacks chlorophyll, lives closely associated with fungi, and supports its branching stems on shrubs; its reddish flower clusters bear small, hairy flowers.
A tall, single-stemmed herb native to the Iberian Peninsula and north-western Africa. It flowers once in its life and, in Portugal, grows in dry farmland, abandoned olive groves and roadside banks.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A perennial herb endemic to Madeira, it usually grows on rocky shorelines. It has no stem or only a very short one and bears relatively few flower heads.

A rounded flowering shrub endemic to Banks Peninsula in Canterbury, New Zealand, it has erect stems and narrow, light-green leaves. It colonises sunny disturbed places and flowers in summer, sometimes into early autumn.
A low-growing evergreen shrub endemic to New Zealand’s South Island, from Marlborough to Otago above 3,000 feet. It has thick, closely packed, backward-curving green leaves and white flowers.

An evergreen flowering shrub found in Chile and New Zealand’s South, Stewart and Auckland Islands, koromiko has a drooping, willow-like form. Its narrow green leaves accompany strongly scented clusters of white or violet flowers, followed by downward-hanging capsules.

Evergreen, bushy shrub native to New Zealand—including the Antipodean and Chatham Islands—Patagonia and the Falkland Islands. It has green oval leaves, and branches from Disappointment Island were used by Dundonald shipwreck survivors to build a coracle and oars.
A flowering plant endemic to New Zealand. It was traditionally used in Māori medicine, and koromiko was also used to line hāngī and flavour cooked meat.
edibilityNote: Traditionally used to line hāngī and impart flavour to cooked meat; the passage does not say the plant itself was eaten.

summary: An evergreen shrub native to New Zealand. It has thick, shiny, dark-green leaves and dense pale-pink to bright-magenta flower clusters whose two long projecting stamens create a whiskery appearance.

An annual plant endemic to the southern Iberian Peninsula, it inhabits crop meadows and traditional dry-farmed olive groves on basic clay soils. As assessed for mainland Portugal during 2016–2019, only three population clusters were known in Baixo Alentejo, and it was considered Critically Endangered there.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A spreading evergreen shrub native to Portugal, western Spain, southwestern France and Morocco. It has grey-green leaves and bright yellow spring flowers, sometimes with a maroon blotch at each petal’s base.

A small evergreen shrub native to Madeira, Bystropogon punctatus is rare there and grows mainly along edges and clearings of laurel forest. Its branching stems bear aromatic, usually serrated leaves and small flowers ranging from white to purplish violet.
A perennial herb, Hypericum glandulosum showed topical anti-inflammatory and pain-relieving activity, as well as antidepressant properties, in a mouse study.
A climbing plant endemic to the Azores. It has leathery dark-green leaves with tiny marginal spines and shiny black fruit when ripe, and occurs on every Azorean island except Graciosa.

A low-growing herbaceous perennial native to eastern Russia, northeastern China, Korea and Japan, it is a clump-forming succulent with star-shaped yellow flowers and russet-red autumn fruit. Its young leaves and stems may be eaten cooked.
edibilityNote: Young leaves and stems may be cooked and eaten.

summary: A dense-branched shrub native to mountain regions of France and the Iberian Peninsula. Its leaves fall early, often leaving bare stems, while its yellow flowers can colour broad mountain slopes and produce a strong honey-like scent.

A slender tree or shrub native to southern and southeastern Australia. It has drooping reddish-brown branchlets, blue-green to grey-green foliage and spherical golden to pale-yellow flowerheads, blooming throughout the year but most heavily from September to January.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.

Perennial herb native to Eurasia and Siberia, now introduced to North America. Its pink flowers have deeply divided petals that create a memorably ragged appearance, while downward-pointing stem hairs make it rough to the touch.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on coastal dunes and sandy deposits in the floodplains of large rivers.

sources.title: Rumex roseus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A tree native to central and southern China, Korea and Vietnam, silkworm thorn bears mulberry-like edible fruit that can also be made into wine. In China, its leaves feed silkworms, while its bark supplies paper and reddish-yellow dye.
edibilityNote: The edible fruit is grown occasionally and can be used to make wine.

summary: An evergreen shrub endemic to the Canary Islands of Tenerife, La Gomera and La Palma. It has spirally arranged, toothed leaves and clusters of orange-red flowers; it also contains toxic cardiac glycosides.

An evergreen shrub from Madeira, with toothed leaves and summer clusters of yellow, orange or russet flowers, often patterned with chocolate-brown markings. It favours wooded slopes and cloud forests, often near water.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Ulex micranthus grows in scrub on acidic ground. It is much more common on schist than granite.
A flowering plant native from Mexico through Central America and South America as far south as Argentina. It has become an invasive weed in Australia.
An annual grass native to mainland Portugal, Trisetaria panicea occurs in fallow land, meadows, cultivated fields, waste ground, roadsides and walls.

A perennial herb of unspecified native origin, the cut-leaved dandelion has lobed leaves with usually sickle-shaped, toothed side lobes. It bears pale-yellow flowers and reddish-brown fruits, and in Germany grows in dry grassland, sheep pasture, vineyards and along roads.

sources.title: Taraxacum lacistophyllum (Dahlst.) Raunk.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Taraxacum sundbergii is a dandelion for which no habitat information is supplied.
Flowering plant present in Portugal; its subspecies conimbricensis is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Teucrium lusitanicum subsp. lusitanicum is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Euphorbia oxyphylla inhabits scrub clearings, open woodland, roadsides and banks on disturbed or stony acidic soils. Its latex is particularly toxic.

A herbaceous plant recorded very locally in coastal, south-central and eastern Spain and North Africa. Its several stems rise from a partly woody base, with leaves crowded near the base and more widely spaced above; dense flower clusters appear from June to July.
A red alga of unspecified native origin, it has a flattened, much-branched reproductive form with opposite side branches of alternating unequal lengths. Another phase forms a low, spreading crust.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Tuberaria plantaginea grows in pastures, annual meadows, waste ground and scrub clearings. It favours acidic, especially sandy, soils.
An annual grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Periballia involucrata grows in sparse mountain grasslands on acidic ground.
A clover whose subspecies willkommii is native to mainland Portugal.

A grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Anthoxanthum amarum is chiefly a woodland plant of cool sites near water, including deciduous woods, scrub and moisture-loving meadows. It is centred in the peninsula's northwest, with an isolated eastern population.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it belongs to the nettle family. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Union legislation.

A perennial flowering herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows mainly in shady woodland habitats on deep, acidic soils. Its long, soft leaves and uniformly dark-brown bracts help distinguish it from the similar Asphodelus ramosus.

A tree, or sometimes shrub, native to northeastern Argentina, southern Brazil and Paraguay, northwestern Uruguay and southern Bolivia. It bears small greenish-white male flowers and pink female flowers on separate plants, followed by fruits whose retained sepals turn from green to red and are valued ornamentally.

A deciduous shrub or small tree native to the Azores, Europe and the Middle East. It bears flat clusters of ivory flowers and drooping clusters of glossy, dark purple-to-black berries. The flowers have a long culinary tradition, while the berries are mildly poisonous raw but edible after cooking.
edibilityNote: Flowers are traditionally used in drinks and fritters; berries are mildly poisonous raw but edible after cooking. Seeds and green parts contain cyanogenic glycosides.

summary: A small leguminous tree or thorny shrub native to Peru, especially associated with coastal desert fog oases. Its pods are rich in tannins used for leather; seed-endosperm gum is a safe food thickener, while flour from the seed germ is potentially toxic and banned from US food.
edibilityNote: Seed-endosperm gum is safe as a food additive; flour from the seed germ is potentially toxic and banned from US food.

summary: A flowering plant species native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant whose subspecies daveaui and langei are native only to the Iberian Peninsula and occur in mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it inhabits dry, open meadows, pastures, cultivated ground, olive groves and extensively managed orchards.

A small annual flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and western France. It has blue-green foliage and tiny white or off-white flowers in spring and summer, growing in dry, open, sunny places.

A flowering plant endemic to central mainland Portugal, it grows in grasslands, roadsides, fields, scrub clearings and rocky crevices on silica-rich ground. Its present distribution and population size remain poorly known because it is often confused with similar plants.
A flowering bush native to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa, Stauracanthus boivinii occurs naturally in Portugal, Spain, Morocco and Algeria.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it is associated with sandy coastal scrub. It grows on stabilized dunes and coastal cliffs, only rarely beneath pine or cork-oak woodland.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in dry scrub and open pine or cork-oak woodland. It favours acidic sand on coastal dunes and cliffs but also occurs on sandy deposits inland.

An evergreen shrub native to the western Mediterranean Basin, including Iberia, northwestern Africa, southern France, Italy and several Mediterranean islands. It has small, drooping, bell-shaped flowers ranging from yellowish white to reddish brown and grows in varied Mediterranean habitats, including semi-arid places.
Erica plant endemic to the Canary Islands and Madeira. It includes the subspecies Erica platycodon subsp. maderincola.
Flowering plant native to Spain and mainland Portugal. It can grow with shoots at ground level or complete its life cycle within a year.
A heath endemic to the Azores, Azorean heather grows mainly on coastal cliffs, lava flows, dry slopes, in natural forests, ravines and craters, from sea level to the islands’ highest elevations.

A perennial deciduous grass native to the Atlantic coast of the Americas from Newfoundland to northern Argentina, saltmarsh cordgrass dominates some brackish coastal marshes. Its sharply tapered leaves bend at the tips, while flowers and seeds grow on only one side of the stalk. At marsh edges, it extends into the water and accumulates sediment.

A herbaceous perennial cordgrass that originated in southern England around 1870, common cordgrass is a hybrid-derived neonative in Britain. Its flowers and seeds grow on only one side of the stem, while spreading rhizomes can rapidly form invasive colonies across tidal mudflats.

Perennial grass native to salt marshes along the southern South American coast. It forms upright clumps without rhizomes, with narrow gray-green leaves rolled inward and dense, spike-like flower heads. Introduced populations can become troublesome marsh weeds, including in California.

Coarse perennial cordgrass native to western and southern European coasts and western Africa, with a separate population on the Atlantic coasts of Namibia and South Africa. It spreads from a creeping rootstock in sheltered saltmarsh mud, shingle and dried pools. Green in spring and summer, it turns light brown in autumn and winter.

A perennial cordgrass native to the Atlantic coast of the Americas, from Newfoundland to the Caribbean and northeastern Mexico. It forms thick mats of slender, wiry stems, with inward-rolled leaves and deep-purple flowers arranged on one side of the stalk.
An annual grass native from south-central Europe across to North Korea, and also in the Sahara, it grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Sporobolus aculeatus (L.) P.M.Peterson — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

summary: An annual grass native to Europe, the Middle East and North Africa. Its mostly upright, unbranched stems are often dark, and its dense cylindrical flower cluster contains tiny green to purple spikelets.

An annual grass native to Europe, it forms low mats and clumps near water. Its green stems and chunky, club-shaped flower heads are tinged purple, while broad leaf sheaths partly cover the flower heads.
Flowering plant native to Madeira.

A bush or small tree naturally found across western Europe, North Africa and some Mediterranean islands. It quickly colonizes poor soil and also grows beside waterways, on beaches and in waterlogged ground.
A small daylily native to northern Asia, including Siberia, Mongolia, China and Korea. It bears broad, scentless yellow flowers. In China, the flowers are eaten as a traditional food.
edibilityNote: The flowers are eaten as a traditional food in China.

summary: A deciduous tree native to the temperate and subtropical Himalayas and Indochina, Morus indica may also grow as a shrub. Its young branches have fine, soft hairs that disappear with age, and its compound fruit turns black when fully ripe.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it has been introduced to Madeira. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Union legislation.

A woody-stemmed flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows mainly on inland, sandy acidic soils in uncultivated ground, slopes and rainfed crops. Its upright stems branch strongly from the base and bear rigid, angular branches. The plant is reported as toxic to humans and ruminants.
edibilityNote: Reported toxic to humans; the source does not specify a plant part or preparation.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A shrub or small tree native throughout the Mediterranean and the Arabian Peninsula. Its smaller branches have reddish bark, and its adult, scale-like leaves press closely against the twigs; unlike a similar juniper, it produces pollen in autumn.

An evergreen shrub or small tree native to the western Mediterranean region. Seedlings have needle-like leaves that become scale-like on older plants, while orange-brown, berry-like female cones mature in about 18 months and are mainly dispersed by birds.
edibilityNote: The berries are used as a cooking seasoning and to flavour alcoholic drinks, particularly gin.

summary: An Iberian-endemic shrub with a narrow form, slightly drooping branches and brown bark that peels in thin layers. Its needle-like leaves usually grow in threes, while its cones ripen over two years from yellowish to red or copper-red.

sources.title: Juniperus navicularis Gand.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An evergreen fern native to Europe, western Asia, northern Africa and western North America. Its broad, wavy sterile leaves contrast with narrower fertile leaves bearing two thick rows of spore-producing structures underneath. The roots, shoots and leaves can be cooked as famine food.
edibilityNote: Roots, shoots and leaves can be cooked as famine food.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to southwestern Europe, specifically Portugal, Spain including the Balearic Islands, and France. It is typically found in the subtropical zone.

An annual succulent native to Macaronesia and regions from the Mediterranean to the Arabian Peninsula and Iran. Its above-ground parts are densely covered with small bumps, and its forked stems are brittle. Solitary flowers appear from January to June, with green outer and white or yellowish inner segments.
Flowering plant in the St. John's wort family, native to Europe. Larvae of the moth Euspilapteryx auroguttella feed on it.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. It occurs in scrub clearings, meadows, annual pastures and cultivated fields, mainly on limestone; its capsule reportedly has conspicuous thick ridges, though this feature needs confirmation.

A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal, it occurs locally on stabilized sandy soils in the centre and southwest, forming two subpopulations. Portugal’s 2020 Red List assessed it as Vulnerable following surveys conducted from 2016 to 2019.

summary: A flowering thistle endemic to mainland Portugal, Cirsium welwitschii is restricted to the subcoastal belt between Baixo Vouga and southwestern Alentejo, chiefly on permanently waterlogged ground. Its stem leaves are often poorly developed or absent, while its basal leaves are comparatively well developed. It is rare, with widely separated populations that are usually very small.

summary: A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal. It grows in very wet places such as damp meadows, peat bogs and marshes, with a scattered range from around Grândola to Gerês.

summary: A rush endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula, it grows in moist, nutrient-poor sandy soils. In mainland Portugal during 2016–2019 it was assessed as Vulnerable, with fewer than 10,000 mature plants estimated nationally and an inferred continuing decline of at least 10% over the preceding decade.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced in the Azores. It favours damp or shady coastal sites, often on sandy ground that floods periodically or beside ponds; its leaf stalks may be tendril-like, though this feature needs confirmation.

A low-growing perennial with two varieties documented as native to mainland Portugal. It grows in scrub clearings and pastures on disturbed acidic ground; var. latifolia may also occur on dunes and coastal rocks.

An annual flowering plant native to Mexico and Guatemala and naturalised in many other countries. Its many cultivars have velvet-textured yellow, orange or russet flowers. In Georgian cuisine, the dried, ground petals are a pungent, earthy spice known as Imeretian saffron.
edibilityNote: Dried, ground petals are used as a spice in Georgian cuisine; florets can also colour human foods.

summary: Seaweed recorded along the Western Australian coast from north of Perth to the Kimberley region.

An evergreen, semi-evergreen or deciduous shrub found in the central and eastern Himalayas and southern and central China. It has leathery or paper-like leaves and includes three accepted varieties with distinct regional ranges.

A flowering herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Knautia subscaposa grows in scrub clearings on dry, basic soils. During Portugal’s 2016–2019 assessments, its mainland population comprised two isolated subpopulations with very small groups and fewer than 250 mature plants.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An annual flowering plant represented in mainland Portugal by two native subspecies. Both occur in dry annual grasslands in fallow land, rain-fed orchards and roadsides, particularly on basic, somewhat nitrogen-rich ground, and may be parasitized by Cuscuta planiflora.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. It grows in annual meadows and pastures, including fallow and agricultural fields, waste ground and scrub clearings.

A small annual herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Valerianella multidentata grows on dry limestone soils in open, sunny or cleared places. During 2016–2019, it was known in mainland Portugal from only one subpopulation on the limestone hills south of Sousel, 320 km from the nearest known Spanish subpopulations.

summary: Deciduous shrub or small tree native to southern China and southern Japan. It typically grows in scrubland and woodland, and its accepted Japanese and Chinese varieties occupy the corresponding parts of its native range.

An upright evergreen shrub, it has narrow, silvery-grey leaves and compact, slightly rounded clusters of pink buds. Its tiny, scented white flowers appear from November to February, with yellowish to reddish bracts.

An evergreen succulent perennial native to Madagascar, it has arching branches with rounded, glossy leaves. Its hanging, urn-shaped flowers range from salmon-red to bright red and appear from late winter into spring.
Evergreen flowering shrub endemic to Chile, with glossy, saw-toothed leaves. It bears clusters of scented yellow flowers in summer and needs a sheltered position in temperate regions.
A flowering tree native to Kazakhstan, the Altai, Mongolia and Xinjiang in China. This poplar readily hybridizes with other poplar species and has high genetic variation.
A flowering tree native to Great Britain, northwestern Spain and Portugal. In Spain it often grows on north-facing valley slopes in mixed forests with common beech.

A small red marine alga recorded from the British Isles, Mauritania, the Canary Islands and the Channel Islands. It is dark purplish red, with irregular cylindrical branches and short, hollow, bladder-like branches.
A multicellular marine red alga found in Europe, Africa and some Atlantic and Pacific islands.

A perennial herb native to fields and meadows of central South America. It grows upright with dense yellow flower clusters, deeply divided leaves that are dark green above and whitish-green below, and small wind-carried seeds with white hairs.
Flowering plant native only to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.

A perennial woody shrub native only to Madeira, Argyranthemum dissectum is highly branched and has deeply divided leaves. Its flower heads have white outer petals and yellow centres. It is quite rare, growing on rocky coastal cliffs and in damp inland places.

A leafy liverwort found in Europe outside the Mediterranean, parts of Asia, northern North America and Greenland. It forms bluish-green to grass-green mats, with leaves usually split into two spiny-toothed lobes and often bearing yellow-green clusters of reproductive bodies near the tips.

A miniature orchid first described from Yunnan, China, and also found in northern Vietnam, Dendrobium hekouense inhabits foggy evergreen forests in subtropical highlands. A single flower emerges from a leafless pseudobulb, and in its natural habitat it flowers in August or September on the ground-facing side of tree trunks.

A very spiny tree native to eastern and northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Cuts in its bark release fragrant resin that dries into small clumps, while its flaky outer bark can be silvery, reddish or bluish-grey over green inner bark. The resin is used to flavour meat products, desserts, soft drinks, gum and sweets.
edibilityNote: Its resin is used to flavour meat products, desserts, soft drinks, gum and sweets.

summary: A multicellular marine red alga of unspecified native origin, it is found across parts of Europe, Africa, Australia, Russia, Alaska, the Philippines, Colombia and some Atlantic islands. It forms maerl beds in shallow coastal waters from Portugal to Norway, providing habitat and shelter for many fish and invertebrates.

A large shrub or tree from South America, it inhabits gallery forests along major rivers in northeastern Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Its finely textured, yellow-ochre wood is used for precision and ornamental objects.

A low-growing annual native to Europe, Western Asia and North Africa, it has weak sprawling stems and usually scarlet flowers, though blue and pink forms also occur. Its flowers open in sunshine and close under overcast skies.
edibilityNote: Experimental oral doses of liquid from the plant caused intense nausea, headache and bodily pain in humans for 24 hours.

summary: A scrambling subshrub native to central South America. Its hairy, grey-downy leaves look dull or velvety, while vivid reddish-orange flower clusters bloom through summer into autumn and attract hummingbirds.

A low-growing annual herb native to central and southern Europe, it has weak, sprawling square stems and paired bright-green leaves. Its small, usually blue flowers have conspicuous yellow anthers and appear from April to October.

Low-growing perennial of unstated native origin, it occurs in damp habitats across western and southern Europe and Northwest Africa. In the United Kingdom it is now mostly restricted to the western half, though it was formerly more common in the east.

A succulent coastal shrub naturally occurring in Australia and New Zealand, beaded samphire grows in salty, often wet habitats. Its young jointed stems are fleshy and bead-like, sometimes red-tipped, but become dry and woody with age.
edibilityNote: The plant is described as edible and known to have been consumed by humans.

summary: A salt-tolerant glasswort native to southern Europe, North Africa, Western Asia and Yemen, it grows in saline conditions. It was the principal saltwort used to make a special potash from Mesopotamian times to the early Islamic era.
A flowering bromeliad of unspecified native origin, typical of Brazil’s Atlantic Forest in Espírito Santo, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro. It is often grown as an ornamental.
A flowering plant endemic to southern Brazil.

sources.title: Aechmea comata (Gaudich.) Baker
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). English Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/c3kkgh accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A straggling evergreen flowering perennial native to South America from southern Brazil to Uruguay. It has downy, heart-shaped leaves and pale-blue star-shaped flowers that age to purple, followed by boat-shaped seed pods.
A perennial flowering herb native to Africa, lucky bamboo is not a true bamboo. Its slightly twisted grey-green leaves grow from a fleshy stem, which distinguishes it from bamboo.

A shrub or small tree endemic to eastern Australia, especially rivers, rocky riverbeds and periodically flooded channels. Its flexible branches often droop, with pinkish new growth and summer flower spikes that are usually cream or pale yellow but occasionally pink.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows on shaded, acidic ground in woodland clearings, beside granite walls and paths, and in traditional olive groves.

Annual flowering plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal, its few known populations are scattered in inland Trás-os-Montes and Beira Baixa, growing in short-lived meadows on sand and gravel over rocky outcrops in river flood beds.
