sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A tropical succulent endemic to La Palma in Spain’s Canary Islands, it is little branched or unbranched. Its smooth, blue-green leaves are tinged reddish brown, and its flowers are white or pinkish white.

An erect annual flowering plant native to Europe, Asia and North Africa. Its finely divided leaves accompany broad clusters of white flowers, and its fruit has traditionally been brewed as a medicinal tea in Egypt.

A tree native to tropical and subtropical South America, mainly low, wet areas around the Paraná, Paraguay and Uruguay rivers. Its rough, deeply cracked bark contrasts with purple, pink or occasionally white trumpet-shaped flowers that appear before the leaves, followed by long pods releasing winged seeds.

A short, shrub-like cactus growing along the Texas Gulf Coast and possibly in northern Mexico. It has purplish fruit and unusually shaped pads narrowed like a neck, usually green but rarely blue-green.

An annual flowering herb native to mainland Portugal, it occurs across the Mediterranean on very dry, basic ground. In mainland Portugal it is small and difficult to detect, with only seven scattered southern locations known at the 2020 assessment, when it was classified as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Micropus supinus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Semi-evergreen shrub native to Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, the Himalayas and southwestern China. It has thick stems and dark green leaves, producing clusters of usually six scented yellow flowers in spring and summer. In protected places it keeps its leaves through winter, but severe cold may freeze its foliage and buds.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows along scrub edges, in hedges, olive groves and fallow fields, favouring cool sites with alkaline soils.

A perennial flowering herb native to the western Mediterranean, including Portugal, Spain, Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. It grows in dry open scrub and coastal pinewoods, chiefly on acidic sandy or schist soils.

A long-lived perennial endemic to Madeira Island and Deserta Grande Island, and formerly native to the Savage Islands. Critically endangered, it has a hard, woody, unbranched stem and markedly shiny yellowish-green leaves, and grows on rocky cliffs and soil-filled terraces.

Semi-evergreen shrub native to the Mediterranean region and the Middle East as far as northern Iran. It has yellow flowers, usually clustered at branch tips, and small, round black berries that develop in autumn.

A bulbous flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is currently restricted to one stretch of a stream in central Algarve and is assessed as Endangered following continuing declines in its range, habitat and population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Narcissus willkommii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A tree native to northern Asia, the Korean Peninsula, the Kuril Islands and northern Japan. It can reach 30 metres tall.

An annual herb endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. It grows near the coast in open scrub, pinewoods and annual grasslands on dry, nutrient-poor sandy soils, and is classed as Vulnerable in mainland Portugal.

A tropical flowering succulent endemic to El Hierro, La Palma, La Gomera, Tenerife and Gran Canaria in the Canary Islands. This small branching shrub has short, spoon-shaped leaves with linear glands, smooth branches and golden-yellow flowers.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it is reported in Portugal only from Serra do Cercal, in dry, open scrub and stony ground. Ongoing studies suggest the Portuguese population may be distinct from the Spanish population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Bupleurum acutifolium
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Flowering plant recorded in Portugal, with no species-level native origin stated. Its subspecies Thymelaea coridifolia subsp. dendrobryum occurs in mainland Portugal and is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

A low-growing perennial plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It occurs in mountain scrub clearings on acidic ground, often where Pyrenean oak woods have been degraded; in Portugal it is frequent and abundant within its small northern range.
A flowering plant native to Europe and Asia, ranging from east-central Europe through the Balkans and Turkey to the North Caucasus and European Russia.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in cultivated meadows and occasionally in walls or rock cavities, favouring dry, stony, disturbed soils rich in bases.

sources.title: Platycapnos spicata (L.) Bernh.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An annual flowering herb native from Portugal and Morocco east to the Himalayas. It has waxy blue-grey foliage and pale pink flowers; its seeds are used in Chinese medicine.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Arenaria emarginata subsp. emarginata is native to mainland Portugal.

A deciduous tree native to forests of Bolivia, Paraguay's Chaco region and the Piedmont Mountains of western Argentina. Its swollen, bottle-shaped trunk stores water for the dry season and bears thick woody spines. Ripe fruit splits open to reveal black seeds surrounded by cotton-like white fibres.

A bulbous perennial native to the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado from Brazil to Paraguay. It grows on rocks and trees and bears large scarlet flowers with green throats, usually four per stem, in late summer and autumn.

A plant endemic to northeastern Portugal, restricted to outcrops of ultrabasic rock. In the 2016–2019 mainland assessment, it was Endangered, with fewer than 250 mature plants estimated across six small population clusters.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Antirrhinum rothmaleri
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Succulent flowering plant endemic to El Hierro in the Canary Islands. Its rings of hairy-edged leaves turn purple in summer and green in winter, and it bears whitish-pink flowers with eightfold symmetry.

A perennial, densely branched subshrub found on Lanzarote; its native origin is not explicitly stated. It forms fairly flat rosettes of bluish green leaves, often reddish near the tip, and bears domed clusters of pink-marked whitish flowers.

sources.title: Aeonium lancerottense (Praeger) Praeger
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering succulent endemic to Tenerife in the Canary Islands, it is frequent on the island’s northeastern Anaga peninsula and prefers some shade. Large green leaf rosettes grow from a freely branching woody stem and can make the plant top-heavy.

A tall, columnar cactus endemic to Mexico, with numerous narrow ribs and dark-red flowers clustered near the shoot tips. Its egg-shaped green fruits are covered with scales, wool and bristles and have a delicate, nutty flavor when eaten.
edibilityNote: The green fruits are edible and described as having a delicate, nutty flavor.

summary: An epiphytic perennial native to Ecuador’s rainforests, pink quill forms stemless rosettes of thin, recurved leaves. In spring and autumn it produces paddle-shaped spikes of pink bracts with vivid violet flowers.
Flowering plant native to dry tropical forests of southern Ecuador and northern Peru. It is also planted as a street tree in scattered cities worldwide.

Hardy, tube-shaped bromeliad native to Brazil. Its surface is heavily patterned with silver hairs in bold bands, and the central tube holds water; it bears a hanging red-pink flower cluster with small blue flowers.

A basil species native to Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Sudan and Ethiopia, commonly called camphor basil. Its aerial tissues have distinct chemical profiles; flowers yielded the most putative metabolites in one analysis and stems the fewest.

sources.attribution: Singh P, Kalunke R M, Shukla A, Tzfadia O, Thulasiram H V, Giri A P, felipe (2020). summary: A thorny, scrambling shrub or vine with a mostly pantropical distribution, usually found near coasts. Its spiny pods contain glossy grey seeds that can float and remain viable in fresh water and seawater, allowing ocean dispersal.
Flowering plant native to southern Macaronesia, specifically the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Salvage Islands.

Fern native to Florida, southeastern Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and much of South America. It commonly inhabits freshwater marshes and swamps, and its horizontal rhizomes sometimes climb tree trunks.
A flowering plant with variety-specific native ranges: var. vagans is endemic to Macaronesia and occurs in Madeira, while var. ciliatum is endemic to the Azores.

A flowering plant native to Bahia in northeastern Brazil, it is commonly grown as a houseplant. Unusually for its genus, the undersides of its leaves have a fuzzy, fur-like texture, and it may produce small yellow flowers.

A shrub or tree endemic to eastern Australia. All its parts have a spicy smell, and its contrasting white flowers appear in autumn and winter; it contains the poisonous alkaloid doryphorine and should be treated with caution.

An evergreen shrub considered native to Taiwan, although its wild origins have long puzzled botanists. It has glossy, sharply toothed foliage and scented yellow flowers from autumn through winter into spring, followed by blue or black fruit.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal.
A flowering plant in the dock family recorded in Portugal. Its subspecies maderensis is native only to the Madeira archipelago.
Flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal.

A herb or semi-shrub endemic to northern Madeira, Solanum trisectum is extremely rare and known from a single laurel-forest site. Its stems and leaves are densely glandular-haired, while its pale-purple flowers have yellow pollen-bearing parts in three sizes. Ripe berries are flattened and red-orange or red.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Teucrium heterophyllum subsp. heterophyllum is endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant in the figwort family, native only to Madeira.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal's Madeira Archipelago.
Flowering plant endemic to Macaronesia, with a documented occurrence in Madeira. It is not protected by Portuguese or European Union legislation.
A perennial shrub endemic to Madeira. It has deeply divided, irregularly toothed leaves and numerous yellow flower heads, flowering from April to August.
A flowering plant native to Madeira, Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago, Taraxacum lidianum belongs to the daisy family. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant endemic to the Madeira archipelago.
An annual grass native to mainland Portugal and introduced to Madeira. In Portugal it grows in meadows, fallow ground and annual pastures on dry or seasonally wet soils, avoiding lime-rich ground.
A flowering grass native only to Portugal’s Madeira archipelago.
Perennial grass native to the Madeira archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean. It grows in clumps, with broad, rough-edged leaves and open, oval flower clusters.
Flowering grass endemic to Macaronesia, including Madeira.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A sedge found in the Azores, Madeira and, over 6,000 kilometres away, the mountains of East Africa. It usually grows in mountain forests but sometimes occurs in sunny grasslands.
Green alga found widely in freshwater habitats; its native origin is not stated. It forms curved or contorted single-row colonies whose tapering cells may be arranged in a straight or zigzag pattern.

Low-growing flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits dry, stony openings in scrub, unused ground and pastures; reported traits needing confirmation include leaves in threes and generally flexible stem hairs.
A plant native from the Indian subcontinent to China, it has two accepted varieties as of March 2020.
A deciduous, bushy shrub native to Europe and Asia. It has grey leaves and bears clusters of yellow and coppery-red flowers in summer, followed by green seed pods.
Perennial flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It occurs in pastures and along woodland edges.

An annual flowering herb with no explicitly stated native origin. It is usually reddish, with square stems and lower branches longer than the others; its leaves are usually smooth-edged and green, sometimes reddish-brown.

A perennial grass whose natural distribution is obscured by widespread planting that probably extended its range. It forms tufts, has hairless leaves and stems, and bears an open, more-or-less one-sided flower head from June to August; it is also an important forage crop.

A sprawling, downy plant found across most of Europe east to Iran, parsley-piert grows on fields, paths and bare, often dry ground. Its tiny green flowers have no petals and sit inside leaf-like cups. The slightly acidic leaves are edible raw and were historically recommended for salads and winter pickles.
edibilityNote: The slightly acidic leaves are edible raw; a 17th-century herbalist recommended them for salads and as a winter pickle.

summary: A rhizomatous grass found in Europe and temperate Asia. It is a salt-tolerant relative of wheat, and hybridising the two can produce salt-tolerant wheat.

A plant in the broomrape family with no native origin supplied, eyebright has been used in traditional Austrian medicine. The herb was taken internally as tea or applied as compresses for eye and gastrointestinal disorders.

A flowering plant native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Guyana and northern Brazil, it has broad green leaves striped pink or white, though the pattern often disappears as they mature. In the Amazon, its leaves traditionally line fish baskets and serve as thatch.
A flowering prayer plant endemic to Brazil’s Atlantic Forest, it is widely kept as a temperate-zone houseplant for its ornamental leaves. It needs partial shade, humidity and good drainage.

A tree native to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and northern South America. It commonly inhabits coastal swamps and wet lowland forests, and its exceptionally hard, durable wood has been used for house posts, bridge timbers and shipbuilding.
An evergreen perennial native to Rio de Janeiro state in Brazil. Its slender pale-green leaves have dark blotches above and purple undersides, folding together at night and reopening in the morning.

An annual herb native to Europe, lesser chickweed forms low, yellowish-green patches, mainly in short sandy grassland near the sea. Most flowers have no petals, though a small proportion have five deeply divided petals that never open widely.
Flowering plant whose variety Ononis baetica var. baetica is native to mainland Portugal.
An evergreen plant native to southern China. It produces small black berries resembling blackcurrants, which birds eat and disperse.

Shrub found along the southern Himalayan slopes in Bhutan, India, Nepal and Pakistan, and also on mountain slopes in southern China. It bears bright yellow flowers in spring and fruits that mature from red to dark purple in summer. The fruits are inedible because their seeds are poisonous.
edibilityNote: The fruits are inedible because their seeds are poisonous.

summary: A flowering grass whose documented native origin varies by subspecies. The nominate subspecies is native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but introduced in the Azores, while subsp. thomasii is native to mainland Portugal.

A small succulent subshrub found on La Gomera in the Canary Islands, it grows on rocks and walls. Its rough, branching stems bear loose rosettes of glossy green leaves with red edges, often becoming much redder in full sun, and it produces pink flowers.

A barrel cactus endemic to east-central Mexico, it develops a large, roughly spherical body with prominent ribs and strong yellow spines. Older plants produce yellow flowers around the crown and edible yellowish-green fruit covered in white wool.
edibilityNote: The yellowish-green fruit is edible and covered with white wool.

summary: A flowering shrub of unspecified native origin, Mexican oregano is highly aromatic. It has rough, slightly hairy leaves of varied shapes and small white flowers clustered in heads.

A bulb plant native to the Pyrenees of northern Spain and France, the small-flowered daffodil grows in alpine meadows and scrub. It has solitary yellow flowers and resembles Narcissus asturiensis but has larger stems. Introduced elsewhere in Europe, it has naturalized in Austria.

An evergreen fig native to eastern India, Bangladesh, Indochina, Peninsular Malaysia and Yunnan in south-central China. Its leaves have two distinct forms: narrow on lower sterile branches and broader higher on the plant. In temperate climates it is often grown as a houseplant.
An annual herbaceous plant reported as native to Bolivia. It is the most commonly grown Nicotiana species, with leaves commercially harvested and processed into tobacco for human use.

A semi-annual herb native to South America, from Argentina through Colombia to Guyana, it has narrow green leaves with serrated edges. It bears clusters of yellow flowers around Easter. The plant, or sometimes only its flowers, is made into tea, while the flower heads are used in medicinal wines and bitters.
edibilityNote: The plant or flowers are made into tea; flower heads are used in medicinal wines and bitters.

summary: Perennial grass native to the Mediterranean region and Transcaucasus. Despite being called annual fog and having a scientific name suggesting an annual, it is perennial.
Perennial flowering shrub whose native origin is not stated, recorded in Mexico and the US states of Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi. It can flower from spring until the first frost.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in grassland, pasture and scrub clearings on acidic, stony or sandy soils derived from schist or sandstone.

A flowering plant native to the Great Plains of North America, showy prairie gentian bears blue, pink or white bell-shaped flowers singly above blue-green waxy leaves. Depending on growing conditions, it may grow as an annual, biennial or perennial.

An annual herb native to mainland Portugal and distributed across much of the Mediterranean region. It has solitary blue flowers with pale tubes and distinctly triangular lobes, and grows in dry, clay-rich pastures, field margins and roadsides.

sources.title: Convolvulus humilis Jacq.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An orchid endemic to far northern Queensland, Australia, it grows on trees, shrubs and boulders in mist forest. It bears up to four usually apricot-coloured, sometimes yellowish-green flowers, with tangled white hairs edging the white, purple-tinged lip.
A flowering plant native to Kyushu, Japan. It is a parent of many hybrid dwarf azaleas derived from naturally occurring Kurume azaleas used in bonsai.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in wet mountain grassland and sparse grassland that floods temporarily, over rock, sand or gravel.

Evergreen shrub, rarely a small tree, native from the Himalayas through southwestern China to Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. It has shiny, spine-edged leaflets, large clusters of yellow flowers and spherical deep-purple berries.
A flowering bromeliad native to Ecuador and Peru.

A deciduous shrub native to mountainous regions of Korea and Japan, it bears lacy clusters of blue or pink flowers in summer and autumn; soil acidity affects their colour. Its sweetener-containing leaves are used for regionally popular herbal teas.
edibilityNote: Leaves containing the sweetener phyllodulcin are used for regional herbal teas, including Korean sugukcha or isulcha.

summary: A low-growing, spreading perennial native to coastal southern Africa. It has blue-grey foliage and brilliant yellow, daisy-like flower heads through summer; in colder gardens it is grown as an annual.

A flowering annual plant native to mainland Portugal, Hypecoum littorale also occurs in southwestern Iberia and North Africa. It favours coastal sands and dunes, flowers from March to May, and in mainland Portugal is restricted to scattered sites along the southern Algarve coast.

summary: Shrub originating from Madagascar and now found across Southeast Asia. Its leaves are traditionally taken as a tea or infusion to treat cancer and diabetes.
A shrub endemic to Peru, it closely resembles Fuchsia boliviana. Its sepals spread as the flowers open but remain angled instead of folding fully back against the floral tube.

Annual plant native to the Mediterranean region of southern Europe, northern Africa and the Middle East, as well as Great Britain, the Low Countries and Germany. It is covered in woolly hairs and bears dense clumps of small flower heads.
An evergreen plant, Pilea spruceana has no native origin stated in the supplied information. Known as silver tree, it is low-growing and can spread wider than it grows tall.
Climbing plant found in south-central Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia. Its woody stem becomes reddish with age, and its leaves have five leaflets arranged like a palm.
Plant species native to Spain, Portugal, France and Italy, including some Mediterranean islands. It is notably tiny, usually trailing along the ground, with very small flowers.

A flowering plant endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula, from Portugal’s Algarve to Huelva and Cádiz in Spain. It grows in salt marshes and bears basal leaf rosettes with flower stalks that bloom from May to August.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in annual grasslands within scrub clearings and dry orchards, favouring somewhat disturbed, mainly basic soils.
A tropical succulent endemic to La Gomera in the Canary Islands. This branching shrub has small rosettes of pale-green to yellow-green leaves, usually striped reddish, and greenish-white flowers.
A subshrub native to southeastern and southern Brazil. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

summary: An annual herb with a strong smell, deeply toothed triangular leaves and a pyramidal flower cluster. It occurs across Europe, India and temperate Asia to China, typically on nutrient-rich soils in fields, gardens and waste ground.

sources.title: Chenopodiastrum hybridum (L.) S.Fuentes, Uotila & Borsch
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An annual flowering herb native to southern Europe, Asia and parts of North Africa, it grows on bare mud in coastal or inland salty habitats. It is often low and spreading, with fleshy leaves and green or crimson colouring, and can be difficult to distinguish from red goosefoot.
An annual flowering plant native to southern, central and southeastern Europe, North Africa, and western and central Asia.

An upright lycophyte endemic to the Portuguese archipelagos of the Azores and Madeira. It has narrow leaves with toothed edges and repeatedly forked branches. It grows in damp, sheltered places and is less common in Madeira than in the Azores.

A grass whose native range is not separated from its invasive range in the supplied records; observations span the Americas, southern Asia and scattered parts of several other continents. Its subspecies occur in wetlands, swamps and streams, but also in waste places, gardens and rice fields.

A flowering plant native to humid mountain ranges from southern Europe through the Caucasus and northern Iran, with widely separated populations in Siberia and from the Himalayas east to Korea. In mainland Portugal's 2016–2019 assessment, it occupied wet, nutrient-poor hay meadows in the northeastern highlands and was Endangered, with four identified locations and continuing habitat decline. Abandonment of traditional meadow management and excessive grazing were important threats there.

summary: A small perennial flowering shrub whose native origin is not stated, white burr-daisy grows mainly on clay soils in grasslands and open forests of New South Wales and Queensland. It has white, occasionally mauve, daisy-like flowers and flattened reddish-brown fruits with several spines.

Deciduous tree native to most of Europe, North Africa and temperate Asia. It is typically compact and domed, with nearly white leaf undersides, cream-white May flowers and scarlet berries. The berries are edible when overripe.
edibilityNote: The berries are edible when overripe.

summary: A terrestrial fern native to the warm, humid subtropical forests of South America. It has a robust upright stem forming a trunk-like base and stalked fronds that can exceed one metre in length.

A succulent subshrub native to Brazil, found on rocky outcrops in Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina. Usually growing in groups, it has cylindrical stems covered with straight to slightly curved hair-like spines and bears lemon-yellow flowers.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across the western Mediterranean. In Portugal it is confined to schist mountain ridges in the central region; a 2016–2019 mainland assessment classified it as Vulnerable amid continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Jurinea humilis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A low-growing flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits dry scrub and clearings in cork oak, oak and holm oak woodland on varied substrates.

A mostly deciduous oak native to Portugal, western Spain and Morocco, Quercus estremadurensis has broad, shallowly lobed leaves on short stalks and acorns on long stalks. Mature trees are rarely partly evergreen, while young shoots and branches are hairy.

A densely hairy annual herb of unstated native origin, it occurs in southwestern Iberia and North Africa, mainly on coastal dunes and sandy ground. It has yellow flowers and strongly curved, sickle-shaped pods, flowering and fruiting from April to June.
A shrub or tree endemic to the Canary Islands. It is conservation-dependent.

A perennial deciduous succulent native to Algeria. Its many short woody branches form spreading mats, with grey-green leaf clusters at their tips resembling miniature Joshua trees. Bright yellow star-shaped flowers appear in late summer.

Flowering plant native to Macaronesia and the Mediterranean basin. In Corsica it is considered rare and may be overlooked because flowering is sporadic, its colouring is inconspicuous and it often occupies disturbed ground.

sources.title: Allium longispathum Redouté
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering shrub endemic to New South Wales, chiefly recorded in the Goulburn and Capertee River catchments, with an unverified Brogo River record. It grows on rocky sandstone and has divided, needle-like leaves and silky red-to-orange flowers, usually blooming from September to November.

An aromatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across southern Europe and North Africa. It flowers mainly in summer and grows in dry Mediterranean scrub on limestone or clay soils.

A flowering perennial herb native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa, common hedge-nettle forms spreading patches in grassland, meadows and open woods. Its upright stems bear wrinkled, toothed leaves with heart-shaped bases, and it flowers from July to September.

A flowering plant endemic to the northwestern coast of the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in cracks in coastal granite between roughly Matosinhos and Moledo, where its habitat is declining and it is assessed as Vulnerable.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A perennial woodland grass native to Europe and much of Asia, giant fescue favours damp places and neutral to base-rich soils. It forms loose tufts with hollow stems and purple joints, followed in late summer by loose, nodding flower clusters bearing long bristles.
Perennial flowering herb native to China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Russia, southwest Asia and Europe. Its enlarged, tuber-like roots produce upright stems bearing purple-red flowers.
edibilityNote: The Kalmyks are said to have eaten the cooked root.

summary: A perennial plant found in central and southern Portugal, southern Spain, North Africa and Sicily. Most leaves form a basal rosette, while long stalks carry solitary heads of pale yellowish flowers; flowering and fruiting occur from May to July.

A flowering plant native to Brazil, including the Amazon, Cerrado and Caatinga regions, it is typically found from Mato Grosso to Minas Gerais and Pará to Bahia. Its flowers can be collected from November to February, with fruit collected in February.

A biennial or perennial plant from Madeira, Portugal, the parsnip palm has a woody stem and a spreading crown resembling a New Zealand cabbage tree. It produces numerous white to purplish flowers from November to January in the Southern Hemisphere.
A flowering plant endemic to the Canary Islands.
A carrot-family plant native to the Canary Islands and also found throughout the Mediterranean region. In Malta it is reportedly very uncommon.
A succulent native to South Africa. Its short rounded blue leaves may show reddish or purple tones, and its flowers are creamy white or sometimes yellow.

A succulent native to South Africa, Namibia and Lesotho. Its trailing stems carry glossy, curved leaves resembling bananas. Small, cinnamon-scented white or off-white flower clusters usually appear in late winter or early spring, though they may bloom at other times.

An herbaceous perennial native to Japan, China and Korea, Japanese knotweed forms dense thickets from an extensive underground stem network. Its hollow, jointed stems resemble bamboo, and it bears small cream or white flowers in late summer and early autumn. Young stems are eaten raw or cooked as a spring vegetable, including as a wild food in Japan, and taste like lemony rhubarb.
edibilityNote: Young stems are eaten raw or cooked as a spring vegetable; they are foraged in Japan and used in European restaurant cuisine.

summary: A domesticated plant native to much of China, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Burma and Vietnam, it is used in traditional Chinese medicine, as animal feed and as an ornamental. Its flowers contain abundant fagopyrin, which can provoke phototoxic effects.
A flowering plant native to southern China and Vietnam. Its leaves yield indigo and supplied East Asia’s most important blue dye until Indigofera arrived from the south.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It favours sandy soils in uncultivated fields, field margins, roadsides and coastal sands, although its Portuguese distribution remains uncertain.
An annual herb originating in the warmer parts of the Old World, devil’s thorn has spinach-like leaves. It produces many seeds in hard, prickly casings along its branches and at the stem base.
edibilityNote: Although bitter, its roots and leaves can be eaten.

summary: Moss of unstated native origin. It is excluded from Algeria because the sole reported specimen there was later identified as another species.

sources.title: Tetrastichium fontanum (Mitt.) Cardot
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Pleurocarpous moss.
A shrub or tree native to Taiwan, parts of China and Myanmar. Its long leaves are divided into many paired leaflets, and its egg-shaped berries ripen dark blue to almost black.
An evergreen shrub endemic to China. It bears sweet-scented yellow flowers and purple-blue berries that are acidic, seedy and edible raw or cooked.
edibilityNote: The acidic, numerous-seeded fruit can be eaten raw or cooked and contains vitamin C.

summary: An African violet species native to eastern and southwestern Tanzania.

Tree-growing cactus native and restricted to evergreen forests in several western and southern Mexican states. Its deeply lobed, flat stems resemble a fishbone, while its strongly scented white or pale-yellow flowers open at night. The fruit's interior is described as tasty and reminiscent of kiwifruit.
edibilityNote: The fruit's interior is described as tasty, with green pulp and small black seeds, and reminiscent of kiwifruit.

summary: An annual or biennial flowering plant native from Macaronesia through North Africa to Crete and nearby Gavdos. It has hairy, sometimes purple-tinged stems and divided leaves, with clusters of unequal violet petals. Its fruit bears a notably long beaklike projection.

sources.title: Erodium aethiopicum (Lam.) Brumh. & Thell. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

summary: A flowering subshrub native to coastal areas of the Mediterranean and Red Seas and parts of the Middle East, it grows in salty coastal and inland habitats. It forms clumps of jointed, succulent green stems with tiny, scale-like leaves. Its seeds contain oil being investigated as a possible edible oil source.
edibilityNote: The seeds contain oil under investigation as a possible edible oil source; documented human consumption is not stated.

summary: An annual plant native to North America and Eurasia, red pigweed is usually upright but can spread along the ground. Its often-branched stems may be green, red or rarely yellowish, and its roughly diamond-shaped leaves can be fleshy, especially in brackish conditions.
edibilityNote: The Goshute Shoshone of Utah use the seeds for food.

summary: A deciduous shrub native to China, it is distinguished by hairy leaves and flowers later than other members of its genus.

A herbaceous plant native to the Mediterranean region. Its small, hairy leaves cover stems that lie along the ground, and its inconspicuous flowers and overall grey colour can make it easy to overlook.

Annual flowering plant native to temperate Europe. It has grey-green branched stems and usually intense blue flowers that bloom all summer; cultivated varieties also come in pink, purple, white, lavender and very dark maroon.
edibilityNote: Flowers are eaten raw, dried or cooked; petals colour or garnish foods and are also used in teas and other drinks.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to eastern Australia, it has egg-shaped leaflets and pale yellow to cream flowers. It grows in forest, woodland and rainforest along the coast from Gladstone in Queensland to Lismore in New South Wales.

A flowering aroid whose native origin is not stated. It grows from a large fibrous corm and forms a crown of thick green leaves. In some areas of Southeast Asia and Japan, its leaf stalk is reportedly eaten as a vegetable and used in dishes including miso soup and sushi.
edibilityNote: The starchy root and, in some parts of Southeast Asia and Japan, the leaf stalk are reportedly used as vegetables.

summary: Evergreen vine native to Brazil, with glossy, broad green leaves. Its rose-pink flowers have yellow centres and appear from late spring to early summer.

A perennial tropical shrub native to Espírito Santo and Minas Gerais in southeastern Brazil, Goeppertia concinna has pointed light-green leaves marked with dark-green spots along the central vein. Its short flower cluster carries pointed green bracts and bright-yellow flowers.

A flowering perennial and subshrub native to the steppes and hills of southwestern and central Asia. It has aromatic gray-green leaves and showy blue-to-violet flowers from midsummer into autumn. Its flowers are eaten in salads in parts of Afghanistan and Pakistan, including Kashmir, where they add a sweet flavor.
edibilityNote: Flowers are eaten in salads in parts of Afghanistan and Pakistan, including Kashmir, where they provide a sweet flavor.

summary: A small marine red alga found in the eastern Atlantic from the Shetland Isles and Britain south to Morocco and the Mediterranean. Its upright branches attach by root-like structures and may grow on other algae or on rocks in shoreline pools.

A small marine red alga recorded around the British Isles, Morocco and the Mediterranean. It forms dense tufts of upright branches arranged alternately in one plane and attaches itself with rootlike structures; male and female plants are separate.

A creeping perennial succulent vine native to South Africa's Cape Provinces. Its trailing stems root where they touch, while its small spherical leaves resemble strings of beads and have narrow translucent windows. The vegetation is somewhat poisonous and should not be eaten.
edibilityNote: The vegetation should not be consumed; ingestion may cause minor illness such as vomiting or diarrhoea.

summary: A palm native to southern Brazil and Paraguay, it usually grows in small populations. Its solitary trunk is wrapped in persistent, criss-crossed fibres ending in woody spines, while its fan-shaped leaves are dark green above and silvery beneath.

A small shrub native to Madagascar, Kalanchoe tetraphylla has a stout, unbranched stem and usually two pairs of opposite leaves. Its name is often wrongly applied in horticulture to the southern African Kalanchoe luciae.

A perennial herb native to the Eastern Himalayas, East Asia and Southeast Asia, it grows in clumps from a rhizome-like root. Its flowers usually have five colourful sepals in native habitats, while cultivated plants may have double flowers with around 20 sepals and prominent yellow stamens.

A perennial flowering herb native to China, Taiwan and Vietnam, it is widely cultivated as an ornamental. Its downy foliage surrounds flowers with rosy-purple or carmine sepals and yellow stamens; in its native habitat, it blooms from July to October.

A rhizomatous perennial herb native from Europe into western Asia, wood anemone flowers in early spring and becomes dormant by midsummer. Wild flowers are usually white but may be pinkish, lilac or blue, often with darker colouring on the backs.

A goldenrod endemic to the Azores, Portugal. It has numerous pointed, slightly thick leaves and many small yellow flowers, and occurs across all nine islands in exposed coastal habitats and rough ground.
An annual, partly parasitic herb native to the western Mediterranean. It grows upright with many branches and is densely covered in sticky, glandular hairs; its flowers are usually pale yellow.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A small red alga reported from Ireland and Britain, it has dark purplish-red, hollow branches divided by constrictions that give them a beaded appearance. Its fronds bend back toward the rock and form attachment points where they meet it.

A flowering plant native to the eastern United States, especially the Ozark and Appalachian mountains and Cumberland Plateau. Uncommon across its range, it grows in deep shade beneath cliffs and rock overhangs, often as the only plant with water-carrying tissues there, and flowers from late summer into fall.

A perennial thistle native to the Mediterranean basin, with a pinkish flower head sitting directly among spiny leaves rather than on a stalk. It grows in fields, shrubland, woodland and rocky ground, flowering in late summer or early autumn.
edibilityNote: Ingestion can cause fatal poisoning, including when its gummy discharge is chewed or the plant is mistaken for an edible thistle.

summary: Small evergreen tree or large shrub native to the extreme lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and parts of Mexico. It has dark green foliage and slightly fragrant yellow flowers, usually blooming from February to July and sometimes into October.

A rosette-forming plant from the eastern Carpathians and the mountains of the Balkan Peninsula. Its flat, open rosettes carry leaves varying from green to brown or red, sometimes with white edges. It usually grows on limestone and produces a few closely clustered offshoots by rosette division.
An aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits cold, shallow, nutrient-poor rivers and smaller streams with neutral or acidic water.

An orchid found in peninsular Thailand and Malaysia, Annandale's Bulbophyllum has conical pseudobulbs, each carrying one succulent leaf. Flower spikes grow from their bases and bear two to four small yellow flowers.

A free-floating perennial aquatic plant native to tropical and subtropical South America, common water hyacinth has bulb-like, buoyant leaf bases and spikes of lavender-to-pink flowers. It grows extremely quickly, forming mats that can double in size within one to two weeks.
edibilityNote: Green parts and flowers are eaten in Taiwan, Java and Vietnam, usually cooked; harvested plants can absorb contaminants and be toxic.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on disturbed, trampled ground beside paths, especially on limestone or dolomite soils.

A spiny, much-branched shrub endemic to the southern Iberian Peninsula, from Portugal to Jaén. Its stems end in spines and its flowers occur singly or in pairs; it inhabits heath and scrub on thin soils over slate or granite.

Semi-succulent perennial native to southern and eastern Africa, the Arabian Peninsula and India. Its fleshy, hairy leaves have a pungent oregano-like smell and sharp mint-like taste; the strongly flavored leaves are used as an oregano substitute and to season meat in the Caribbean.
edibilityNote: Strongly flavored leaves are used as an oregano substitute and to season meats in the Caribbean.

summary: A low woody flowering plant whose listed varieties, var. gracilis and var. ramosissima, are native to mainland Portugal. It chiefly grows in sandy scrub on coastal dunes and cliffs, occurring more rarely in abandoned dry orchards or river alluvium.
An evergreen fern native to Japan, Taiwan and Korea.
A tree native to Georgia, Florida and South Carolina. It has pale grey or brown ridged bark, long leaves with pointed, toothless leaflets, and sheds its leaves in early spring.

A short-lived tree native to most of Europe, southwest Asia and northern Africa. Its rounded young leaves and buds are sticky, while its female catkins mature into woody, cone-like structures that persist through winter.
An herbaceous grass from the Mediterranean region. It grows in annual grasslands, wasteland and scrub on sandy or limestone ground.

sources.title: Avellinia festucoides (Link) Valdés & H.Scholz
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering grass recorded from Portugal, with native origin specified only for subspecies livida, which is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

An annual grass native from the Canary Islands and Madeira across the Mediterranean and Western Asia to India, and also to South Africa’s Cape Provinces. It has twisted awns and was probably used in the Persian festival of bahmanagān.

A non-spiny evergreen shrub endemic to the central and western Iberian Peninsula, including northern Portugal. Its upright green-grey branches bear yellow flowers in spring and early summer, and it forms large stands on sunny mountain slopes with granite or quartzite soils.

A fern endemic to the Azores, Azorean spleenwort occurs on all nine islands. It has leathery, plastic-like fronds and a very thick, glossy, dark garnet central stalk, and grows in terrace walls and north- or northwest-facing volcanic rock crevices.
A herbaceous fern endemic to the Azores, it grows in plantations, ravines, mountain slopes and laurel forests. Invasive plants compete with it and alter its habitat.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal.

An evergreen tree endemic to New Caledonia, where it grows in dense humid forest. Its large, stiff, leathery leaves form tufts at branch ends, and its flowers have a sweet scent. Individual trees are male or female.

A rough-haired perennial herb of unstated native origin, it occurs in northern Iberia and French Cerdanya; southeastern Swedish populations may not be native. It grows in pastures, meadows, stream margins and roadsides, bearing yellow flowers and numerous hairy fruits.

sources.title: Geum hispidum Fr., Fl. Hall.

summary: An annual grass endemic to Santa Maria in the Azores, it forms dense tufts. Its leaves are thickly hairy on both sides, and its oblong flower clusters contain compact spikelets.
A flowering plant endemic to the Azores, where it occurs on four of the nine islands. It grows in upland meadows, shrubland, cliffs, slopes, woods and roadsides.
A plant endemic to Santa Maria in the Azores.
A flowering grass endemic to the Azores archipelago.

An emerald-green moss of unstated native origin, it grows on sunny, lime-poor ground that is moderately moist or dry. Its nearly upright capsule has a densely felted cap, and its spores mature in winter.

sources.title: Pogonatum nanum (Hedw.) P.Beauv.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A perennial herb of unstated native origin, it is found in the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa. It has an underground tuber and grows mainly in sandy pastures, cork-oak woods, holm-oak woods and pine woods.
A decorative perennial grass native to northwestern Asia and North Africa. It forms clumps of pale pink flower plumes that mature to brown and needs protection from prolonged freezing weather.

Orchid occurring in humid deciduous woods of westernmost Europe. In mainland Portugal it currently has two widely separated subpopulations and is assessed as Endangered, with an estimated 143–250 mature plants and continuing habitat decline.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A perennial flowering plant endemic to the western Iberian Peninsula, it is very rare and occurs in western Portugal and Galicia. It grows in warm, very wet or seasonally flooded vegetation and has deeply grooved fruit with prominent finger-like warts.

A leafy moss found across Europe, Macaronesia, Turkey, the Caucasus, North Africa and North America, especially in Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean regions. It forms loose, soft yellow-green mats; its leaves spread when wet but lie close or twist when dry. Spore capsules are very rare, while reproductive bodies are abundant.

Spiny shrub endemic to the extreme southwest of mainland Portugal. It grows in low scrub on coastal clifftops or nearby flats and was assessed as Vulnerable after only eight locations were identified amid continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Ulex erinaceus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A compact, upright succulent herb endemic to the high Peruvian Andes. Its thick, U-shaped leaves have translucent upper windows and change from bright green in shady summers to reddish in dry, sunny seasons.
A grass native to the western Mediterranean, including southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa. In Portugal it inhabits dry, sandy meadows and clearings.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Apomictic dandelion native to Iberian mountain ranges, with current presence confirmed in Portugal’s Serra da Estrela but still uncertain in Gerês. Its leaves are purple-spotted with strongly recurved, toothed lobes, and pollen is scarce and limited to the outer flowers.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Taraxacum estrelense
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering tree native to Portugal and Spain. It grows in riverside and other wet habitats and is related to the common alder.
An evergreen flowering plant native to the Caribbean and cultivated as an ornamental. It has fleshy shoots, rounded light-green leaves and inconspicuous flowers packed into long, dense spikes.

sources.title: Peperomia trifolia (L.) A.Dietr.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A multicellular marine red alga found in Europe, Africa, Brazil, Australia and some Atlantic islands.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal, it is confined to a few siliceous rocky deposits high in Serra da Estrela and has a very small population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Rumex suffruticosus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An arum-family plant native to the Atlantic Forest, it is found in Paraguay and southern and southeastern Brazil. Its leaves lack holes and have finer, wavier divisions than those of Monstera deliciosa; the plant is moderately toxic, especially its leaves.

Flowering succulent with no explicitly stated native origin; it occurs from the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa to Sicily. Its papillate leaves and preference for gypsum and limestone distinguish it.
Staghorn fern found in Australia.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There it grows in scrub clearings, woodland edges and perennial grassland, generally on limestone soils.

summary: A low, spreading herbaceous perennial native to central and southern Europe, North Africa and western Asia. Its pale yellow flowers have reddish veins, while its four-winged, sword-shaped fruits become brown, woody and brittle when ripe.
A moss native to Europe and China. In Iceland, it is known from only two locations on palagonite cliffs and is classified there as vulnerable.

A perennial herb with no stated native origin, found across much of northern Iberia and the western French Pyrenees. It has a rounded underground tuber and white flowers, and occurs chiefly beneath oak, beech and pine woodland, but also in meadows, clearings and rocky ground.

A freshwater red alga with no stated native origin, recorded in Europe, China and North America. It forms dense blackish-purple tufts of mostly unbranched, hollow threads and grows on submerged stones and wood in clean, cold headwater streams.

summary: An evergreen thorny shrub native from the Mediterranean basin eastward to the Arabian Peninsula and Iran. Its tangled branches commonly become spines, while its tough leaves vary greatly in shape from rounded to narrow and needle-like.

summary: Woody plant native to the Canary Islands and Madeira, off northwestern Africa.

An annual vine native to South and Southeast Asia, sponge gourd bears cucumber-shaped fruit that turns brown and strongly fibrous when fully ripe. Young fruit is eaten as a vegetable, while ripe fruit is inedible and used as a scrubbing bath sponge.
edibilityNote: Young fruit is eaten; shoots, flowers and leaves can be cooked, mature seeds roasted, and edible oil extracted from seeds.

summary: Flowering plant native to temperate and subarctic parts of the Old World, from scattered African countries across nearly all of Eurasia to New Guinea. Common mouse-ear chickweed is one of the world’s most widespread weeds and has been introduced to many regions worldwide.
A moss with an almost worldwide distribution. It can grow under artificial light in places lacking natural light, including Crystal Cave in Wisconsin.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in dry meadows, pastures, scrub clearings and pine woods, especially on coastal sandy soils.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Silene gracilis is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant with no native origin supplied, it grows in openings among salt-tolerant scrub in Portuguese estuaries and salt marshes. It favours sandy, salty soils.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it inhabits dry, rocky or somewhat disturbed places around woodlands, scrub, banks and fallow ground. It is the only known host of the parasitic plant Orobanche nepetae.

An annual herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa, it grows in fairly shaded scrub on slopes. Its branching stems bear tendrils, pink flowers and two contrasting fruit forms: lower one-seeded fruits and upper two-seeded fruits, often with hooked tips.

A flowering herb native to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa, Galium viscosum grows in fallow land and traditional rain-fed olive groves on basic soils. In mainland Portugal, it was assessed as Vulnerable in 2020, with small, widely scattered populations in the south.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the south-western Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal only around the Monchique mountains. Portugal's population was estimated at fewer than 350 mature plants and thought to have declined by more than 60% since 2001, with eucalyptus plantations and their management identified as the main pressure.

summary: A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in mainland Portugal only along the southern Algarve coast, in openings and scrub edges on loose sand. During 2016–2019, only three current Portuguese locations were identified, and the species was assessed as Endangered there.

summary: An evergreen tree native to Macaronesia and endemic to the Canary Islands and Madeira, it is part of laurel forest. It has glossy dark-green oval leaves, often bearing mite-induced galls, and elongated fruits that become blackish when ripe.

A perennial flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe and North Africa. Its vanilla-scented, pinkish-mauve flowers appear in winter, and deep rhizomes allow it to spread extensively on shady roadside banks.

Tree endemic to south-eastern New South Wales, where it grows in wet, high-rainfall forests on hills and plateaus. It has rough bark low on the trunk but smooth upper bark that often peels in ribbons, plus narrow curved leaves, white January flowers and conical or bell-shaped fruit.

A leafy liverwort distributed across northern parts of the Northern Hemisphere, from Europe and the Arctic to Asia and northern North America. Its green to brown-green shoots form sturdy mats or grow among other mosses, with asymmetrical leaves divided into three very unequal lobes. It occupies moderately shaded sites on rock, soil, tree bases and, rarely, dead wood.

A shrub-forming cactus endemic to Bolivia, it has upright light-green stems branching from the base. Yellowish-white flowers emerge from a long, dense structure of reddish-brown to gray wool and numerous spines.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula; no habitat information is supplied.

A small red marine alga with no native origin stated, it is recorded from Ireland, Great Britain, the Channel Islands and France. It forms branched tufts with strongly curled tips and banded-looking, spineless filaments.
A small marine red alga of unstated native origin, found around parts of Europe and eastern North America. It forms highly variable tufts and grows on other algae as well as artificial materials.

Perennial flowering herb native to Western and Central Europe, including the British Isles. It has white flowers with five petals split about halfway, and long, narrow grey-green leaves on roughly four-angled stems.

A small marine red alga found around Ireland, Britain, the Isle of Man, Norway, France and the Mediterranean. Its branches have strongly curled tips and distinctive three-celled spines. It grows on rocks, shells and other algae.

A deciduous willow shrub native to northern North America, tealeaf willow has green leaves with whitish undersides and produces flower clusters before its leaves emerge in spring. Its young spring leaves may be eaten; Inuit people also ate the leaves and shoots raw, dried, or stored in seal oil, and used the leaves for tea and soup.
edibilityNote: Young leaves may be harvested in spring; Inuit people ate leaves and shoots raw, dried, or stored in seal oil, and made tea and soup.

summary: A perennial grass native to Asia and Australia, it forms graceful, spreading clumps. Its narrow green leaves turn golden yellow and then beige, while arching, brush-like flower spikes change from silvery or pinkish white to brown as seeds form.

An orchid endemic to the Philippines, it naturally inhabits moist subtropical or tropical lowland forests. This robust plant sometimes hangs downward and can bear up to 30 strongly fragrant flowers in autumn.
A low-growing perennial herb native to South Africa. Its young leaves are hairy, and its white flowers have a slight pink tinge before turning yellow with age.

A climbing cactus native from Mexico to Honduras. Its scented flowers open at night, and it is widely cultivated as both an ornamental vine and dragon-fruit crop. Its red fruit has white or, less commonly, pink pulp and edible black seeds.
edibilityNote: Cultivated as a dragon-fruit crop; the red fruit contains white or occasionally pink pulp and edible black seeds.

summary: A flowering plant native to every Canadian province except British Columbia and nearly all the United States except the Pacific coast states and Nevada.
A flowering shrub native to Jamaica and introduced to Madeira, Réunion and the Society Islands. It produces masses of pink flowers throughout the year.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it grows in farm-associated or nutrient-rich meadows. Possible identifying features, still requiring confirmation, include flower clusters with only two rays and highly divided upper leaves.

A deciduous shrub with no native origin supplied, it occurs on Madeira and the Canary Islands. Its yellow flowers have a strongly sweet fragrance and are picked shortly after opening for fresh extraction of essential oil used in perfumery.

Epiphytic evergreen perennial endemic to Espírito Santo in eastern Brazil. It forms basal rosettes of strap-shaped leaves and arching clusters of tubular red-and-yellow flowers followed by berries. It does not tolerate freezing temperatures and is often kept as a houseplant in temperate regions.

Succulent shrub native to South Africa. It has brittle branches and blue-green to blue-grey leaves that are flattened sideways and marked by translucent lines. Its usually knife-like leaves distinguish it from the similar Curio talinoides, whose leaves are rounded in cross-section.
Flowering plant native to Cuba and Jamaica. It tolerates shade and is grown as a houseplant or outdoors in warm climates.

An upright flowering tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It grows in shady forests and thickets and has slightly inrolled leaves, elongated pyramidal flower clusters and white bell-shaped flowers.

A perennial subshrub native from the western Mediterranean through North Africa to the central Sahara. It has a woody base, conspicuously hairy stems and leaves, and reddish-purple flowers striped with white.

An annual, occasionally biennial herb native to the western Mediterranean, Albania and Macaronesia. Its solitary flower heads generally hang before flowering, and its brown fruits occur in two markedly different forms.

A large perennial bunch grass native to Africa and Yemen. It can withstand wildfire and drought, and may reproduce by cloning itself through seed. In some regions, including South Texas and Hawai‘i, it is an invasive weed and fire hazard.
An evergreen shrub native to South America, mainly Argentina and Uruguay. Its yellow flowers have conspicuous long crimson stamens, while its seed pods are covered in short red glandular hairs.
edibilityNote: The seeds and green seed pods are toxic and can cause severe vomiting and other abdominal symptoms.

summary: A thorny tree native to parts of Morocco, southwestern Algeria, Mauritania and Western Sahara. Its gnarled trunk supports a wide-spreading crown, while its hard nuts contain oil-rich seeds; the fruit is eaten, and oil from gently roasted seeds is used with bread, couscous and salads.
edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten; oil from gently roasted seeds is traditionally used with bread, couscous and salads.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal, it occurs only around Serra de Nogueira and Sabugal, along oak-woodland edges and clearings. During mainland Portugal's 2016–2019 assessment, it was classed as Endangered, with about 120 mature plants in four known groups and an inferred continuing decline.

summary: An annual flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in sandy soil with temporary moisture beside paths and in meadows and pastures.

A perennial plant native to Tanzania, Malawi and Mozambique, it grows in rocky crevices. Its fleshy, pale green leaves may have reddish markings and purple edges, while its many flowers are pale greenish to lilac with purple veins.
A miniature epiphytic orchid endemic to Ecuador’s coastal provinces. It lacks pseudobulbs and has a fan of red-green leaves, with elongated flower clusters bearing pink buds in winter and spring.
Dwarf succulent native only to South Africa. It has a thick, fleshy body with many green, often curved, spiny branches radiating from the top and leaves that fall off.
A daisy native to western Europe, Algeria, Morocco and Spain. Unlike the similar Bellis sylvestris, its seeds have scales on the pappus.

A European blackberry species whose scientific name is ambiguous: its type specimen matches Rubus plicatus, but the name has also been applied to broader groups. Under a source using the name Rubus fruticosus, its fruits are used in desserts, preserves and sometimes wine.
edibilityNote: Under the source's use of the ambiguous name, the fruits are made into desserts, preserves and sometimes wine.

summary: A perennial shrub native to Brazil's Atlantic Forest region, especially Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, it grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical habitat.

A perennial sedge endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, associated with low-altitude marshes and peat bogs. In mainland Portugal it is known from only four locations between Minho and Baixo Alentejo and was assessed as Endangered.

summary: An annual or short-lived perennial found across tropical and subtropical parts of several continents, it commonly grows in gardens, fields, roadsides and disturbed ground. Its daisy-like flower heads have tiny yellow centres and may have white or cream outer petals; young leaves can be eaten as salad, while fresh or dried leaves are also boiled.
edibilityNote: Young leaves may be eaten as salad; fresh or dried leaves are boiled. Older leaves may taste unpleasant and upset the stomach.

summary: Perennial shrub native to arid and semi-arid parts of the Middle East, North Africa and southern Europe. It is greyish and much-branched, with tiny, scale-like hairy leaves and pinkish, winged flower parts.
A flowering plant native to Central and Southern Europe.

summary: A bulb-forming perennial native to Morocco and Algeria, it smells like garlic or leeks. Its flowers are pollinated by bees and other insects.

A stone plant native to the Cape Provinces of South Africa, the Carmine Fingerfig has violet-purple colouring on the undersides of its petals. It is also a notably successful naturalised stone plant in Malta’s natural habitats.
Flowering plant native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and adjoining parts of Brazil. It grows in wet tropical forests and is commercially available as a houseplant.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and restricted globally to the Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa. In Portugal it grows in rocky grasslands on basic soils and is known only from three populations in the Upper Douro basin, though its current distribution is uncertain.
Upright Eurasian herb occurring from Portugal to Japan. It has narrow, roughly hairy, stemless leaves and single yellow flower heads at the tops of thin stems.
A fern native to Macaronesia, Mediterranean Europe, North Africa, western Asia and parts of the Sahara.

A plant native from western France to the western Mediterranean. Its flowers are bright yellow above and paler beneath, with a small white-tipped tooth, while its small oval leaves grow in hairy clusters.
A perennial grass of unspecified native origin, sea couch has a self-supporting form and simple, broad leaves. It is invasive in Mont-Saint-Michel Bay, where it has altered the area's ecology.

A perennial cereal grass of the Old World, distributed across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Its pointed grains are shiny black, and the millet can be ground into meal and prepared as porridge.
edibilityNote: The millet grain can be ground into meal and prepared as porridge.

summary: An evergreen flowering plant native to French Guiana, Bolivia and Brazil. It has large, velvety silver-green leaves with prominent veins and clusters of purple five-petalled flowers; older leaves often turn orange before falling.

An evergreen shrub or small ornamental tree native to southeastern Brazil. It has dark green, velvety leaves with prominent lengthwise veins and large royal-purple flowers, with some blooms throughout the year and the greatest abundance from May to January.
A moss recorded frequently in northern Algeria. It was also found in the colon of the Tyrolean Iceman.

summary: A medium-to-large moss found worldwide in moist or wet habitats. It has feather-like branches and is especially common in lowland Great Britain.
A moss native to the Northern Hemisphere. Its leaves range from yellow to a coppery yellow, and it has been recorded frequently in Algeria.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to the west coast of mainland Portugal, where it grows on sea cliffs exposed to fog. It was assessed as Vulnerable after southern populations disappeared during the past century, with invasive plants and cliff erosion contributing to continuing habitat decline.

summary: A moss of unspecified native origin, recorded across Europe, parts of Asia, North Africa, North America, the Canary Islands and Madeira. It forms loose yellow-green to dark-green cushions, usually on trees, and its leaves draw loosely against the stem when dry.
A flowering plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula, Arabis stenocarpa belongs to the cabbage family and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A moss of the Northern Hemisphere, marsh forklet moss grows in cold springs, wet fens, and along streams and ditches. It forms soft yellow-green to green mats that break apart easily, with leaves bent distinctively backwards.
Flowering plant native to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil.

A perennial herb native to Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama. Its dark green, velvety leaves carry a light green saw-toothed band along the central vein, while its bracts change from white to deep purple over time.
A moss whose native origin is not stated. It has a wide-ranging distribution across parts of the Americas, Europe and Asia, with a particularly strong presence in the eastern United States.

A small marine red alga of unspecified native origin, recorded around parts of Atlantic Europe and nearby islands. Its cylindrical branches appear banded, curl strongly inward at their tips and bear single-celled spines.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it is recorded only near Vimioso, where about 75 mature plants occur in two groups on disturbed limestone soils, and it is assessed as Endangered.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: Annual herb native to the Mediterranean Basin in Europe and North Africa, and to western and central Asia and Pakistan. It has hairy, glandular, branching green or purplish stems, with solitary pink or purplish flowers distinguished by a long, ribbed tubular calyx.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows and pastures on poor, stony or sandy, acidic and somewhat moist soils.
An orchid known only from Mount Kinabalu in Malaysian Borneo.

A plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula and Canary Islands, it is restricted in Portugal to the northwest. It inhabits shaded, damp ravines beneath deciduous woodland and also pit walls. During the 2016–2019 mainland Portugal assessment, it was declining and considered Endangered, with only four known locations.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in scrub clearings on coastal sands and readily hybridizes with Tuberaria guttata.

A flowering plant whose two listed subspecies are endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In mountain areas, subsp. humilis inhabits granite crevices, while subsp. odorata grows in sparse grassland on sandy, granite-derived soils.

A bunchgrass native to the Iberian Peninsula and Morocco, giant needle grass has narrow grey-green leaves and may remain evergreen or semi-evergreen depending on climate. Its tall flower spikes emerge silver-lavender in late spring, turn golden in summer and persist tan into winter.

A low-growing, semi-evergreen subshrub native to the Mediterranean Basin from Portugal to Turkey and south to northern Africa, it has fuzzy silver leaves. Its white flowers are veined pinkish-red, followed by reddish-brown seed pods.

A herbaceous perennial with a broadly Mediterranean distribution, prostrate Canary clover has woody stems, five-part hairy leaves and clusters of small white flowers. Its fruits are reddish-brown pods containing one or two seeds.

An evergreen flowering perennial native to the Amazonian basin of northwestern Brazil, it forms clumps of pale seafoam-green leaves edged and streaked with dark green. The leaf undersides are dark reddish-purple, while cultivated varieties may have nearly black, pink, red or white foliage.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed around the Mediterranean. It inhabits waterlogged clay and muddy soils; during Portugal’s 2016–2019 assessment, its few known locations and continuing national decline led to an Endangered rating.

summary: A perennial shrub or vine native to the Chinese provinces of Sichuan, Yunnan and Guizhou and to western Indochina. It belongs to the legume family and bears orchid-like flowers.
A non-climbing perennial shrub endemic to central mainland Portugal. It grows chiefly in scrub and uncultivated ground, flowering from January to June.

An ornamental plant native to Rio de Janeiro state in southeastern Brazil, Goeppertia louisae has pointed, oval, dark green leaves with silvery light-green bands beside the central vein. The leaf undersides are usually purple, while the flowers are fully white.
